It's great street sea food, you choose the type of snail that will be served to you with noodles and vegetables, and a side dish of roasted shrimps / shells / langostinos depending on your choice (30.000 - 60.000 dong depending on which one you choose). Chosen by locals and no English spoken, so you'll probably have to use a translation…

spots.name: Hanh Pancake
spots.desc: This is a family restaurant where locals come to eat Hue specialities. About half of the guests are Western tourists these days, and a set sampler menu is available.
spots.price: Ban khoai, 20,000-25,000 dong; nem lui, 80,000 dong, bánh bèo 60,000 dong (Jan 2018)

spots.name: La Carambole
spots.desc: Serves French food, Vietnamese food and pizza. Quite touristy.

spots.name: Hot Tuna
spots.desc: Recommend the chicken breast with mushroom sauce and mashed potatoes well worth it. Duck also quite nice.

spots.name: Ong Tao
spots.desc: Excellent traditional Hue food, try the meat rolls (wrapped in mint leaves) or the fried spring rolls. Incredibly crunchy. Not too crowded. On the first floor. All dishes available as small and big portions, so you can order a few.

spots.name: Ancient Hue Royal Cuisine and Gallery
spots.desc: One of the biggest restaurants in the city. Prices are good, food is excellent, extremely clean. It is also a complex of ancient houses among a huge garden area. Nice food carvings.

spots.name: B4 Bar-Café
spots.desc: A charming Belgian-Vietnamese owned bar, with a welcoming interior and free pool.

spots.name: Brown Eyes Chillout Bar-Club
spots.desc: Live DJ, free pool table and a good vibe. Not far from Pham Ngu Lao, but they offer to pay for taxis from hotels for parties of four persons or more. Stays open till the last one passes out.

spots.name: Sinh To Place
spots.desc: Shop for drinking ice tea, coffee, smoothies and juices. Local prices (they are published on a board). Try rau má juice: reputed to be very good for your health.
spots.price: Rau má (centella asiatica juice) 6,000 dong, smoothies (sinh to) 8,000 dong

spots.name: Vy Da Xua
spots.desc: Enjoy a delicious cup of Vietnamese coffee, or any beverage, in this beautiful setting. The traditional beam house is surrounded by a garden and small stream where you can hear birds and restful music.

spots.name: Garden river Bar coffee
spots.desc: Bar coffee in the center of hue You can enjoy your drink and listen music near to the river inside the amazing garden. A Vietnamese and French team will be here to helping you.

spots.name: La Beaute
spots.desc: Lovely cafe on a quiet side street and therefore still unspotted by the LP crowd. Atmosphere with soft music and green bamboo around and half the prices than in the tourist area 200 m around the block. Lots of different coffees and cakes, where especially the very recommendable coffee with cacao flavour is not easy to find in Hue.

spots.name: Sidewalk Coffee
spots.desc: Go local and try some delicious early morning coffee with chocolaty overtones, hot or iced, while watching river life on the canal. The woman who brews it up also offers banh mi, French bread with your choice of fillings. Another woman shares the same area of pavement and sells very reasonably priced banh canh, a popular local breakfast soup. Very clean. After your coffee, you walk along Bach…

spots.name: Po Nagar Cham Towers
spots.desc: These four brick towers were built by the Cham civilization between the 7th and 12th centuries to honour Yang Ino Po Ngar, mother of the kingdom, and the aroma of incense emanating from within makes it clear that this remains a religious site for the local Buddhists of Nha Trang today. The longevity of these last vestiges of a once-dominant SE Asian civilisation should impress temple enthusiasts…

spots.name: Long Son Pagoda
spots.desc: At this pagoda, you will see a 24-m-tall white Buddha. The pagoda was established in 1963 to honour the monks and nuns who died demonstrating against the Diem government. Beware of scammers claiming they are students studying in the temple, demanding that you offer a donation to the school before going up the pagoda. These students have no affiliation with the school and entry to the pagoda is…

spots.name: Nha Tho Nui Cathedral
spots.desc: On a hill overlooking the city, the cathedral shows the influence of French Catholicism. The Nha Trang area still has a strong Catholic population. There are Catholic shops around the cathedral.

spots.name: Alexandre Yersin Museum
spots.desc: This is a scientific museum of Swiss-born Dr. Alexandre Yersin (1863-1943), who arrived in Vietnam in 1891 to study infected animals. He later produced a serum from horses and buffaloes. In this museum, you will be able to view all of his work as well as his equipment. Yersin never went back to Switzerland and spent the rest of his life in Nha Trang. Don’t try to take pictures. Do respect the…

spots.name: Khánh Hòa Museum
spots.desc: Exhibition presents Cham statues and artifacts of the ethnic minorities of the Nha Trang area. One of the rooms is devoted to Ho Chi Minh and his personal belongings.

spots.name: National Oceanographic Museum of Vietnam
spots.desc: This is like an aquarium with popular and rare species of the sea. A good place to bring kids as they will get to see sharks, turtles, coral reefs, lion fish, sea horses, and many other creatures.

spots.name: Impressions Museum
spots.desc: Not really a museum. 3D art paintings to interact with. Great for selfie addicts, but don't go alone! Ideally go as group of 3 or more. Two is OK, but it will be difficult to take photos of the two of you together. Not easy to find, it's on the other side of the old airport from the main tourist area. Receives mixed reviews, many consider it over-priced.

spots.name: Diên Khánh Citadel
spots.desc: Citadel was built by French officer Olivier de Puymanel for Nguyễn Ánh in 1793. It housed royal palace, private houses, warehouses and jail. It was fenced by walls of 3.5 m height, surrounded by moats of 4-5 m deep and 10 m wide. It was built with 6 gates, but only 4 of them remain.

spots.name: Fairy Spring waterfalls
spots.desc: Fairy Spring is a small, cool stream and swimming hole much visited by local kids on weekends. The swimming hole is at the end of a short jungle walk. It is a pleasant place to visit in summer. In winter the water is too cold to swim. The stream's source is the area of Hồn Bà, the highest peak in the province. Bottled and canned drinks are available, but no food is sold here yet. The area is…
spots.price: 10,000 dong per person, 3,000 dong per motorbike

spots.name: Ba Ho Waterfalls
spots.desc: A series of three waterfalls and a fast flowing river tucked away in the forest. There are limited amenities, although you can buy food like rice, chicken, beers and soft drinks. Taxis are available in Nha Trang to take you there, but it's not too difficult to find yourself and with good weather it's a pleasant drive, if you are confident on a motorbike. It's a good one hour trip from Nha Trang…

spots.name: Hon Ba Nature Reserve
spots.desc: At the summit of Hon Ba mountain at 1,514 m above sea level.

spots.name: Monkey Island
spots.desc: Catch a ferry to Monkey Island (the pier is 1 km further north of island), which is full of monkeys, has a 10:00 circus and simple go-cart track.

spots.name: Swimming pools
spots.desc: People come here to swim in the sea, but there are also a number of swimming pools. Louisiane Brewhouse has a good one that is free to use. Hiring a soft chaise longue costs 40,000 dong. The Yasaka Saigon Nha Trang Hotel coffee shop in Yersin St has a small shady pool for free use. A number of mid-range hotels also have pools, some of which can be used by non-guests. Sea and Sun Hotel has a nice…

spots.name: Water Puppet Theater
spots.desc: Water puppetry is a Vietnamese original folk art that dates back as far as the 11th century when it began in the villages of the Red River Delta area of northern Vietnam. Today's Vietnamese water puppetry is a unique variation on the ancient Asian puppet tradition.

spots.name: Gyms
spots.desc: There is a large gym in town called Nha Trang Body Building Club, part of a leisure complex that includes badminton and tennis courts, basketball area and football pitch. Daily pass 20,000 dong; monthly pass, 200,000 dong. Besides, Novotel Hotel also has gym memberships for non-guests, which provide access to the swimming pool, sauna and relaxation room. A daily pass costs 200,000 dong, one-month…

spots.name: 10 pin bowling
spots.desc: On the 3rd floor of the Nha Trang Centre shopping and entertainment complex.

spots.name: Nha Trang Beach
spots.desc: The city's main beach, south of the Cai river, is about 6 km long and lined with a beautiful, well-maintained promenade containing walking paths, gardens, monuments and leisure spaces. The beach itself has a broad strip of sand, and the calm waters are extremely inviting for swimming - but care is needed, as the waters get deep very quickly. While Nha Trang's beach is hardly one of the most…

spots.name: Bai Duong Beach
spots.desc: North of the Cai river, Bai Duong beach is smaller than in the main tourist area. It is a beautiful beach, but the sewage channels make it somewhat less appealing. The beach is mostly popular among Vietnamese visitors, and hence quite empty during peak sunshine hours. Near the beach there are several seafood restaurants catering to Vietnamese tourists. It can be reached using bus #4.

spots.name: Hon Chong
spots.desc: Scenic rock formations in the sea. The disposition of the rocks, as well as the sculpture of a giant fist mark in one of them, is mysterious and a source of several folk tales. You can climb the rocks and get some nice views of Bai Doung Beach and the nearby islands. It can be reached using bus #4.

spots.name: Hòn Tre island
spots.desc: Has several nice beaches, but almost of all them are of exclusive access to guests of the Vinpearl resorts. The exception is the small beach in front of the Vinpearl Land's waterpark, which is accessible for those who bought a ticket to Vinpearl Land. The beach offers waterports and contains a Russian restaurant.

spots.name: Doc Let Beach
spots.desc: Located in the Ninh Hòa district north of Nha Trang, Doc Let is a beautiful, long beach with shallow, crystal-clear waters. The water has weak waves, but it is still excellent for swimming. Local fisher families sell and prepare seafood they will cook for you on the beach for a very reasonable price. The southern part of the beach contains the Ninh Hòa fishing village, where the north of the…

spots.name: Long Beach
spots.desc: It's in the Cam Lâm and Cam Ranh districts, 20 km south of Nha Trang. Bai Dai is in the middle of a frenetic process of development, with upscale resorts being built nonstop in the beachfront. Even so, the beach is very long and it is still possible to find yourself alone if you walk enough. It has beautiful blue waters, soft sand and it is pleasant to walk upon as it is less steep than the beach…

spots.name: Vinpearl Amusement Park
spots.desc: From the harbour you can take the cable car over to the island where Vinpearl Resort and Vinpearl Land are located. They have a small tivoli and some restaurants, attractions here include Underwater World (aquarium), water park with water slides and wave pool, amusement park with roller coaster, pirate ship, bumper cars, cinema, arcade machines and a laser show at night time, usually 19:00. All…
spots.price: Adult 600,000 dong; children under 1.4 m tall 450,000 dong; elderly above 60 430,000 dong; children under 1 m: free

spots.name: 100 Egg Mud Bath
spots.desc: Amusement park featuring mud baths, pools, hydrotherapy showers, jacuzzi and a big garden.

spots.name: I-Resort
spots.desc: Offers mud and mineral baths, waterfalls and a lot of pools.

spots.name: Thap Ba Hot Springs and Mud baths
spots.desc: Costs 50,000 dong for the hot swimming pool and waterfall, 100,000 dong for shared mud bath (if you are 5-8 people you will probably get put in the same tub), shower, hot/cold water jets, hot Jacuzzi, and the hot waterfalls and swimming pool. A massage by trained masseuses and entrance to the hot swimming pool costs 150,000 dong. There is also a package for 500,000 which included a massage among…

spots.name: Yang Bay tourist park
spots.desc: At the Yang Bay waterfalls the Vietnamese have built up a concrete beach, and sort of eco park with a zoo. It used to be a lot nicer before they built it, but it is still a very nice place to visit. You can swim there, and walk around in the area. Just to mention, tourist park receives a lot of negative reviews.

spots.name: Hòn Tằm
spots.desc: The only mudbath services on island in Vietnam. It takes about 6 minutes from Tam pier to the Hon Tam island by cano. The entrance fee is from 350,000 vnd (15$) for full-package service.
spots.addr: Hon Tam island - Vinh Nguyen ward

spots.name: Biking and Rafting Tour
spots.desc: Combination fast 30-km downhill biking passing through an ethnic village and meeting Raglai people. Then a 12-km rafting trip down the Cai River.

spots.name: Central Market
spots.desc: The typical Vietnamese market with fruits, veggies, meat, fish, etc. found in every corner of Vietnam, even though a little more expensive than in other cities.

spots.name: Nha Trang Center
spots.desc: Shopping and entertainment complex. On the 3rd floor is a multiplex cinema, 10 pin bowling alley, a games arcade and a BBQ Da Lat buffet. On 2nd floor has roller blading rink. On the ground floor are KFC, Texas Chicken and Starbucks Coffee.

spots.name: Gold Coast
spots.desc: Shopping and entertainment complex. The 7th floor is the entertainment level with 10 pin bowling alley, games arcade and Kids Camp. On the 3rd and 4th floors is a large 2 level Lotte Mart supermarket.

spots.name: Sunsport Sportwear Stores
spots.desc: Major brands available: Nike, Adidas, North Face, Speedo, Greg Norman.

spots.name: Vincom Plaza
spots.desc: 4-level beachfront shopping complex opened in August 2018 with cinema on the top floor.

spots.name: Go!
spots.desc: Large supermarket on upper floor of big shopping mall, outside the center of town.

spots.name: Mini Mart
spots.desc: This long established family run corner store is very good value and has an amazing selection of items for such as small shop. They are cheaper that the many A-Marts in the area which are very much aimed at the tourist market and few locals will be seen shopping in them.

spots.name: MoonMilk Supermarket
spots.desc: There are several outlets now with good value fixed prices. Sells a lot of health food items not often found in other markets such as Kefir and Greek yoghurt, sourdough bread, matcha power, blueberries, frozen berries, dates, various nuts, kombucha health drinks, quality dark chocolate. Daily specials for near sell by date items.

spots.name: Huyền Hương - Bánh Căn 37
spots.desc: A friendly family serving mixed or pure plates of Bánh Căn with 6 pieces and mango salad at no extra charge.

spots.name: Mì Quảng 82
spots.desc: Not so authentic dish, but the eatery is very authentic though.

spots.name: Bánh Căn Ba Thua
spots.desc: Good Bánh Căn, a unique taste, special fish cakes and a delicious cake soup.

spots.name: Lac Canh
spots.desc: What’s different about this long established restaurant (25 years) is that you get to cook, yourself, and both locals and tourists seem to love it. It's famous for its thinly sliced beef, marinated in chilli source that you cook with your own mini tabletop BBQ. Large San Miguel bottled beers are served by San Miguel-attired servers for 18,000 dong.

spots.name: Truc Linh 2
spots.desc: Asian and Western food. Especially popular for seafood. Truc Linh has been here for years but the original corner one is now the location of a new high rise hotel.

spots.name: Nha Trang Seafood
spots.desc: Serves fresh and scrumptious seafood. Inexpensive prices and good service.

spots.name: Louisiane Brewhouse
spots.desc: Microbrewery with locally brewed beers, restaurant with fresh cakes and tarts, sushi, quality pizzas, steaks, Vietnamese food and seafood. Pool table, live music and own loungers right at the beach or pool available. Chaises longues at either the pool or beach are 40,000 dong per day. Even if you get a chair on the beach, you still have pool access. They have a sampling tray of beer for 100,000…

spots.name: Sailing Club
spots.desc: This restaurant serves Japanese, Indian, Vietnamese, and Italian food. Crowded at night, when it turns into bar.

spots.name: Alley Cafe
spots.desc: Cheap drinking bar and cafe popular with English-speaking expats.

spots.name: Altitude Rooftop Bar
spots.desc: For a great view of Nha Trang at night, perhaps visit the second highest bar in Nha Trang.

spots.name: Skylight Nha Trang
spots.desc: 360˚ skydeck & rooftop club. Besides, it also features a skywalk, pool deck and an international restaurant - Chef's Club on the 43rd floor.
spots.price: Entrance 50,000-250,000 dong depending on time and day of the week, price includes 1 drink

spots.name: SinhTo20
spots.desc: This place has a very good yoghurt and many kinds of cocktails. Prices are reasonable.

spots.name: Why Not Bar
spots.desc: Long-running and still one of the most popular late night bars for the young Western backpacker crowd in Nha Trang. It's been transformed into a much more upmarket establishment and is more popular with Asian tourists.

spots.name: Sữa hạt Green-T
spots.desc: Green T nut milk is made entirely from nature with nuts: Lotus, Walnut, Cashew, Sesame, Almond, bringing the whole thing, suitable for everyone in the family. Green T nut milk is made with all hearts and enthusiasm with the desire to bring quality, complementary and safe products to everyone in the family, especially children and adults.
spots.addr: 36/1 Nguyễn Duy Hiệu, phường Vĩnh Hòa, thành phố Nha Trang

spots.name: Alpaca Coffee
spots.desc: A small homestyle cafe with a good-quality Italian and Mediterranean food and drinks. They also have vegetarian and healthy food. Located upstairs above the green A-mart store. 20% off drinks when ordered with a meal. Its more of an eating place and often gets full, so the drinks discount is probably there to deter customers just buying drinks only.

spots.name: Iced Coffee
spots.desc: Coffee shop in similar style to the large chains such as Starbucks and Costa Coffee, i.e. espresso styles, lots of comfy seating inside and out with upstairs seating too. They also sell cakes and pastries and have a small food menu too.

spots.name: Lava Coffee
spots.desc: More of a Vietnamese-style coffee shop but with both comfortable air-con and alfresco dining areas.

spots.name: Nuoc Mooc Spring Eco Trail
spots.desc: Transportation can be negotiated to take you there from Phong Nha village. Buy a ticket at the hut under the sign off the road, then wander the bamboo bridges and paths along both sides of the river/rapids. Go back to see where the river springs up out of the ground. This is also on the road to the Thien Duong (Paradise) Cave.

spots.name: Hang Toi
spots.desc: A real adventure cave, still without the lights and large tourist groups to spoil the experience. Explore this spectacular cave on a National Park tour or independently, and after kayaking across the river, enjoy swimming through the cave with your headtorch leading the way, then explore a side passage. Hang Toi is a wonderful and very accessible example of the beautiful caves that are found…

spots.name: Ruc Mon Cave
spots.desc: Discovered in 2016 by a local man, this cave has the potential to be the 2nd biggest cave in the world. The first tourists experienced this cave in 2017. Green Land Tours is the only company that offers access to each of the cave's two entrances. The tours are led by the man who discovered the cave and spent 2 years exploring it. The Ruc Mon Cave is named after the indigenous people who made a…

spots.name: Phong Nha Caves Tour Center
spots.desc: Tailor-made tours in Phong Nha Ke Bang National Park, including group tours, daily departures.

spots.name: Gecko Restaurant
spots.desc: Phong Nha Gecko Hostel and restaurant with Cycles bar. Phong Nha's brand new premiere hostel in Phong Nha tourist center - Great spot in town with many options of delicious Vietnamese & Western dishes.
spots.addr: Phong Nha, Son trach, Bo trach, Quang Binh

spots.name: Paradise Pizza and More
spots.desc: Casual dining atmosphere with the best pizza and sandwiches in town. Very good, reasonably priced specials. Free delivery in town, take-away available on all dishes.

spots.name: Gecko Bar
spots.desc: A great place to unwind after your day's adventure. And as the late hours approach quench your thirst with a cocktail at Cycles Bar open late every night.
spots.addr: Phong Nha, Son trach, Bo trach, Quang Binh

spots.name: Vinh Recreation Centre
spots.desc: Indoor pool, cinema, gym, children's playground, arcade and karaoke machine.

spots.name: Colonial Palaces
spots.desc: The three palaces and summer home of the colonial era, last emperor of Vietnam Bao Dai, which is of great interest once you visit these three heritage sites, named Palace I, II and III, the Dalat Palace Hotel being one of them, with its adjacent Dalat Du Park Hotel, all from the 1920s, together with the Dalat Palace Golf Club, which was built in 1922, to give his majesty the opportunity to…

spots.name: Dalat Market
spots.desc: Filled with local specialities: strawberry jam, fruit conserves, avocado, artichokes.

spots.name: Flower Garden
spots.desc: A set of flower gardens centred around a reconstructed traditional Vietnamese teak wood house. If you go for a stroll around the lake, it can be visited as a stop.

spots.name: Truc Lam Zen Monastery
spots.desc: Best to reach it via a cable car ride over the pine forest. Note that both men and women must wear pants and cover their shoulders to enter the monastery.
spots.price: Bus: 7,000 dong, cable car: 150,000 dong both ways, 120,000 dong one way (Feb 2026)

spots.name: Lake of Sorrow
spots.desc: The Lake of Sorrow is a common destination in Dalat. The Lake of Sorrow is so-named because of a tale of two lovers, one who committed suicide after the other was called up to serve in the army.

spots.name: Langbiang Mountain
spots.desc: There are 2 peaks: 1915 m and 2167 m. First one is reachable by a steep paved path, you can ride in a Jeep (360,000 dong for 1 Jeep). The second one is 2-3 hours great hike. You don't need to enter the main gate and pay the fee if going to 2167 m peak, trail start on the right of the gate. Also visit the ethnic village at the foot of the mountain.

spots.name: Linh Phuoc Pagoda
spots.desc: This kitschy temple is one of a kind in Vietnam. Broken porcelain is used to compose beautiful mosaics that adorn the whole of this 7-level pagoda, and it is still expanding.

spots.name: Nha Tho Domaine de Marie
spots.desc: A pink church on top of a hill, with a store selling various dried fruits and snacks from the local orchards run by the nuns of the monastery.

spots.name: Pongour Falls
spots.desc: It's one of the largest and widest waterfalls in Vietnam and during the wet season is a magnificent sight. A dam built nearby has reduced the water flow. Toilets are pit latrines with no water, soap or tissue, so bring your own.
spots.price: 10,000 dong per person. 5,000 dong per bike

spots.name: Prenn Falls
spots.desc: A very common stop on a typical Dalat tour, Prenn Falls is quite beautiful, but is a lot more fun when you're hiking it than just taking pictures of it.

spots.name: Thien Vien Truc Lam Monastery
spots.desc: The monastery has a magnificent view over the dams below and its gardens are full of landscaped shrubs in animal form. Extremely peaceful. A great place to relax and soak in the tranquility. People who do not want to complete the round trip could opt for a 4.1-km walk back to Tran Phu. Be sure to bring a map. On the walk back you can go down to Tuyen Lam Lake, visit nearby Datanla waterfall, and…
spots.price: Free admission. The cable car to the monastery costs 50,000 dong one-way, return 70,000 dong.

spots.name: Tuyen Lam Lake
spots.desc: Its clean green waters flow from the beautiful Tia Spring and from the Da Tam River, which flows down from Voi mountain. Its waters stretch over an immense 350 ha and because of its various sources, Tuyen Lam is known as the lake where rivers, springs, and forests meet. The lake was built in the 1980s. It is one of the largest and most beautiful lakes in town. The other side of the lake is Voi…

spots.name: Valley of Love
spots.desc: The Valley of Love is common stop on Dalat tours and is very popular with honeymooners. The Valley of Love is also a great spot for canyoning.

spots.name: Xuan Huong Lake
spots.desc: Public lake in the centre. Approximately 5 km in length, this lake was made after two dams on the Camly River were destroyed during a storm in the 1930s. Now, Xuan Huong Lake is one of the main draws of Da Lat, and you can see honeymooners and locals strolling its banks. Many nice hotels have a view of the lake. The lake was drained in 2010, but is now filled again. Boats can be rented on both…

spots.name: Lak Lake
spots.desc: Stop on a bike-tour in the central highlands. It's a beautiful ride down to the elephant waterfall through coffee plantations and then up to Lak Lake over a mountain and then through sunny highlands with rice fields. The road is partly very bad, but doable.

spots.name: University of Dalat
spots.desc: Students from the Hand-in-Hand Club are eager to serve as free guides.

spots.name: Dalat (Central) Market
spots.desc: Dalat's Central Market place is the best place in town to eat fresh fruits and vegetables. Near the entrance, there is a lively and always busy vegetable restaurant that serves excellent soups. A tiny vegetarian food stall is in a corner of the second level.

spots.name: Vcafe restaurant
spots.desc: Popular place for Western travellers. Diverse menu of international dishes and live music every evening.

spots.name: Dalat Palace Golf Club
spots.desc: Cafe, pro shop and clubhouse, offering Mexican and Western food.

spots.name: Cafe Noi
spots.desc: Lovely cafe with relaxed music and great coffee with chocolate flavour. Lots of young locals playing cards and board games here. Not yet spoiled by masses of tourists.

spots.name: Cafe Tung'
spots.desc: Really nice cafe. The delicious Vietnamese coffee costs 8,000 dong and is served with tea.

spots.name: Hangout Bar
spots.desc: Classic backpacker bar. Free pool table, board games, and darts. Guests can choose their music. Good place to meet other travellers and expats.

spots.name: Larry's Bar
spots.desc: Library-style decorations with dark wood paneling, pool table, and darts.

spots.name: 100 Roofs Cafe
spots.desc: The main attraction here is the building, which is a themed maze of indoor caves, tunnels, staircases, alcoves, ladders, a rooftop garden and everything in between, while built-in bar tables and chairs are plentifully scattered all around. Definitely not the place to get drunk (unless you sit at the 1st or 2nd floor). Definitely a unique, must-see experience in the city.

spots.name: Thang Hen Lake
spots.desc: Surrounded by mountains, this serene lake is at its best in the rainy season. During the dry season the lake shrinks and is not as impressive, but there are a few rafts that you can take. Walking in the nearby mountains brings you past local herders and farmers. There are no buses to Thang Hen, so the cheapest option is to hire a motorbike driver for the half-day trip. It's about 1 hour away and…

spots.name: God's Eye Mountain
spots.desc: Located within the Non Nuoc Cao Bang UNESCO Global Geopark, this limestone mountain is famous for the large circular hole through its center. The surrounding valley is linked to the Thang Hen lake system and changes strongly with the seasons: in wetter months, water fills the basin, while in drier periods the area can open into a broad grassland landscape.

spots.name: D1 hill
spots.desc: A set of giant stairs. This site contains a monument wall, statue and great views of the valley on all sides.
spots.addr: at Tran Dang Ninh and Duong 7-5/AH13/QL 279

spots.name: The Light House Club
spots.desc: This nightclub serves cheap beer (35,000 dong) and plays improbably loud electronic music.
spots.addr: Mường Thanh Hotel, Võ Nguyên Giáp Road

spots.name: Elephant Mountain An Lao
spots.desc: Elephant mountain An Lao or Núi Voi is a complex of rocky mountains, undulating and meandering. It is around 20 km far from Hai Phong city center. People call this Elephant Mountain as it looks like a reclining elephant. Elephant mountain An Lao is located in Truong Thanh, An Tien and An Thang communes of An Lao district.

spots.name: Haiphong Brewery
spots.desc: Bia hoi, fresh from the brewery that is directly behind this location. Many beer stands here. Look for the bar to the right of the alley where motor bikes are carrying yellow kegs in and out of the brewery. Decent food in an open kitchen. 10,000 dong for a tall glass (500 ml), 4,000 dong for a regular. The beer is pleasant with a slightly sweet aftertaste. Way better than Hanoi beer! Arguably…

spots.name: Amber bar
spots.desc: Upstairs of the Haiphong Brewery. If you are looking for an Amber beer, then this is the place to go. Very delicious, but definitely more expensive than other local beers. 35,000 dong for a tall glass (500 ml), 25,000 dong for a regular.

spots.name: Lý Thái Tổ Statue & Park
spots.desc: The park faces Hoàn Kiếm lake, with a beautiful view of the busy Hang Bai St. and the serenity of the willows on the bank of the lake. Many locals view this mini-park as their favourite place because it is a symbol of the integration of modernity and tradition. One might encounter a group of youths practising hip-hop, breakdancing, or playing foot-badminton, while at the same time seeing a…

spots.name: Fujian Assembly Hall
spots.local: Hội Quán Phúc Kiến / 福建會館
spots.desc: Former assembly hall of the Chinese from Fujian province. It was converted to a primary school after the 1979 Sino-Vietnamese War, but was restored to its former glory in 2015, and is used for some public functions.

spots.name: Canton Assembly Hall
spots.local: Hội Quán Quảng Đông / 粵東會館
spots.desc: Former assembly hall of the Chinese from Guangdong province. It was converted to a kindergarten after the 1979 Sino-Vietnamese War, but was restored to its former glory in 2021, and is now an exhibition space open to the public.

spots.name: Hanoi Train Street
spots.desc: Buildings press up nearly to the railroad ties of the railway through central Hanoi, creating a narrow corridor for trains to pass through. Two stretches of rail corridor, just to the north and the south of Hanoi Station, are lined by restaurants and cafes. Several times a day, trains quickly pass close to the cafe seating. You'll have to buy a coffee, juice or a beer, but prices are reasonable.…

spots.name: Hanoi Train Street (South)
spots.desc: Trains pass several times daily, typically around 10:30, 15:00, and 19:00.
spots.addr: Ng. 222 Đ.Lê Duẩn, Khâm Thiên, Đống Đa

spots.name: Hanoi Sky
spots.desc: Indoor viewing floor at the top of the Lotte Center skyscraper; visitors circle the windows for a panorama taking in West Lake and the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and can step out onto glass panels over the drop.
spots.addr: 65th floor, Lotte Center Hanoi, 54 Liễu Giai, Giảng Võ Ward

spots.name: B-52 Lake
spots.desc: Until 19 Dec 1972, this was just a small brackish pond just off Hoàng Hoa Thám St., about 1 km west of the mausoleum. On that day, in a twisted retelling of the Hoan Kiem legend, Vietnamese anti-aircraft missiles blasted the enemy's eight-engine, 100-ton aircraft and sent it to the shallow bottom of the lake, where it remains.
spots.addr: Ngoc Ha Precinct, Ba Dinh District

spots.name: Downed Aircraft Memorial
spots.desc: A stone plaque commemorating the shooting down of a US Navy (not "USAF" as depicted) aircraft in 1967. Read the Vietnamese script and you can pick out the name of John McCain, the late U.S. senator, one of the airmen.

spots.name: CGV Cinemas (formerly Megastar)
spots.desc: The movies are relatively new, perhaps one or two months later than in the US. The movies are not dubbed although there are subtitles so both non-Vietnamese speakers and locals can enjoy them.
spots.price: 70,000-115,000 dong for 2D movies depending on day and time. 90,000-230,000 dong for 3D movies

spots.name: Hanoi Cooking Centre
spots.desc: Cooking school, retail outlet and beautiful courtyard cafe with an excellent menu of Asian and Western favourites. Hands-on cooking classes and short courses in a relaxed atmosphere.

spots.name: Hidden Hanoi
spots.desc: Hidden Hanoi runs walking tours and cooking classes. There are many options including the 1-hr walking tour of the local market, followed by the 3-hr cooking class. Cooking class menus change daily, and there are other walking tours available. They also run language classes, and there is a dance school in the same building.
spots.addr: 137 Nghi Tam Rd (aka Duong An Duong Vuong), Tay Ho

spots.name: Vietnam Culinary School
spots.desc: Fully equipped facilities to learn Vietnamese cooking. A typical day will commence with a visit to the morning market accompanied by an instructor to select ingredients for your cooking lesson. The class will be followed by a meal in a restaurant sampling your own cooking as well as traditional Vietnamese dishes.

spots.name: SF Salon and Spa
spots.desc: Nice, not too expensive spa with a range of services, including massages, manicures/pedicures, facials. They will pay for your one-way taxi fare to the spa. Friendly staff.

spots.name: VietClimb
spots.desc: 200-m² climbing surface, a 50-m² café & terrace to chill out, and a climbing pro-shop. Also a great place for finding out where to climb immediately outside of Hanoi.

spots.name: Thang Long Water Puppet Theatre
spots.desc: Musicians accompany folk legends from Vietnamese history, told with wooden men, women, and dragons, dancing and splashing on the face of the water. The narratives are sung in Vietnamese, but lyrics are available in several languages. Or just ignore the dialogue and narration and focus on the special effects. There are several performances throughout the day. Don't worry about getting wet, but the…
spots.price: Camera passes are an extra 20,000 dong

spots.name: Hồng Hà Theater
spots.desc: Hát tuồng (Hanoi: [háːt tûəŋ]) or hát bội (Saigon: [háːk ɓôjˀ]) is a form of Vietnamese theatre. Hát tuồng is often referred to as classical "Vietnamese opera" influenced by Chinese opera which combines acting, singing, and dancing. Tuồng employs the use of stock characters who are recognizable from their make-up and costumes, which are typically very elaborate and extravagant. Usually, a…

spots.name: Công Nhân Theater
spots.desc: "Four Palaces” refers to the belief in the worship of Four Mother Goddesses, including Mother Goddess of Heaven, Mother Goddess of Forest, Mother Goddess of Water and Mother Goddess of Earth.The late 19th and early 20th centuries were the most flourishing periods of Mother Goddess religion in Viet folklore. There are times when Mother Goddess religion is considered as a manifestation of…

spots.name: Hanoi Chèo Theatre
spots.desc: Chèo (Vietnamese: [cɛ̂w]) is a form of generally satirical musical theatre, often encompassing dance, traditionally performed by Vietnamese peasants in northern Vietnam. It is usually performed outdoors by semi-amateur touring groups, stereotypically in a village square or the courtyard of a public building, although it is increasingly also performed indoors and by professional performers. Chèo…

spots.name: Chợ Hôm
spots.desc: A huge range of goods, and famous for the fabric market on the second floor. There are many kiosks selling different types of fabrics ranging from cheap, affordable to best quality with a high price. When shopping, take your time and never rush into buying anything. Sellers often quote a very high price that you can bargain down considerably.

spots.name: Chợ Hàng Da
spots.desc: A 6-storey building to house the market is under construction. All the kiosks are now in the neighbouring area, either on Phùng Hưng (second-hand clothing), Đường Thành, or Lý Nam Đế Streets. Sell a huge range of goods including pets, groceries, prepared foods and fabrics. It is now mostly empty.

spots.name: Night Market
spots.desc: The major north-south street in the Old Quarter, from Hoàn Kiếm Lake almost to the train overpass, becomes a crowded walking street with everything from pirated DVDs to traditional ornaments. Prices are negotiable, but "foreigner pricing" is fairly common. Thankfully many shops nowadays offer fixed prices with big "no bargaining" signs.

spots.name: Snake Restaurants
spots.desc: The suburb of Le Mat (aka Snake Village) has numerous restaurants specializing in cobra foodstuffs. Live cobras are stored on the premises much the same way one would find live lobsters at a Western seafood restaurant. If one orders cobra blood wine from the menu, the waiter will take a live cobra, kill it on the spot, drain the blood into a shot glass of rice wine and top it off with the cobra's…

spots.name: Bánh Mì Dân Tổ
spots.desc: The sandwich is very delicious and crispy. Pretty crowded. You can also eat there at 3am and it will feel delicious.

spots.name: Bun Cha Ta Hanoi
spots.desc: Highly recommended if you are looking for authentic North Vietnamese Bun Cha. The food is great, bursting with flavour. Very cosy place.

spots.name: Bánh Mì 25
spots.desc: Vietnamese Sandwiches. This is a good restaurant for a quick bite to eat near Dong Xuan Market. Lovely place and mouth watering food.

spots.name: Little Hanoi Restaurant
spots.desc: Simple Vietnamese home-cooked food. Also amazing vegan food. The fried tofu in tomato sauce and grilled eggplant are delicious. Also a cute date spot.

spots.name: Banh Mi Hoi An
spots.desc: Vietnamese Sandwiches. This place is open from early morning and serves great bahn mi. Nice staff with good English skills.

spots.name: Quán Cơm Bình Dân
spots.desc: Inexpensive, home-cooked Vietnamese meals. Delicious and nutritious rice, clean restaurant.

spots.name: Bún Chả Đắc Kim
spots.desc: Some rate this as one of the best examples of bún chả in Hanoi, and therefore Vietnam (apparently in the south, bún chả is specifically advertised as Hanoi-style). For 100,000 dong each, you'll get a bowl full of tiny minced-pork rissoles that have been chargrilled over an open flame and a massive plate of pork rice paper rolls that have been fried in oil twice. You also get a phenomenal dipping…

spots.name: Pho 10 Ly Quoc Su
spots.desc: Serve delicious beef rice noodle, fried bread stick is crispy and delicious. The place is so clean and nice. All of the soups and sides include beef (bo), so this isn't for vegetarians.

spots.name: Pho Tu Lun (Au Trieu)
spots.desc: Many pho varieties. Store is only open in the morning. Locals crowd the place, so you know it must be good.

spots.name: Com Chay Nang Tam Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.desc: This excellent restaurant is a good vegetarian option, and will please both vegetarians and non-vegetarians with its wide range of innovative dishes, which include fake meat dishes. Restaurant is comfortable with good ambience, and is good value. Well worth the short walk out of the old town.

spots.name: Au Lac Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.desc: Typical local vegetarian restaurant like you'll find everywhere in Vietnam except Hanoi, a little off the beaten track in an atmospheric alleyway.

spots.name: Huyen Huong Restaurant
spots.desc: Choose from a wide variety of seafood dishes (many of which are swimming around in tanks) and other Vietnamese specialities. Friendly staff complements the tasty food.

spots.name: Kaiser Kaffee Restaurant
spots.desc: Interesting little place which has excellent Vietnamese and Western food.

spots.name: Little Hanoi
spots.desc: Upscale cafe serving mainly Westerners in a pleasantly lit restaurant.

spots.name: Mediterraneo
spots.desc: Authentic Italian food, probably the best you'll get in Hanoi. Prices are steep and portions small.

spots.name: Moka Café
spots.desc: Excellent selection of Western and Vietnamese food served in a coffee shop environment.

spots.name: Pepperoni's
spots.desc: Part of a small international chain of pizza restaurants. Locally run, they do regular special offers such as free desserts, eat-all-you-can buffets and loyalty schemes, whereby collecting tokens with each take-out entitles you to a free pizza. Pizzas, burgers, ice cream and apple crumble.

spots.name: 01 -wan- Tantan Ramen
spots.desc: Two-floor ramen shop owned by a Japanese chef, specialising in excellent tantanmen with creamy, Sichuan-inspired "numbing spicy" mala broth.

spots.name: Madam Tu Hong
spots.desc: Restaurant specialising in cha ca (Hanoi-style turmeric-and-dill grilled fish cooked at the table), set in a restored old house once belonging to Madam Tu Hong, a 19th-century Vietnamese businesswoman.

spots.name: Dalcheeni
spots.desc: Authentic Indian restaurant with classy interior and good view of West Lake, frequented by Indian expats; restaurant manager is a Goa native. All meat served is halal, with extensive vegetarian options available. Highly recommend the tandoor-grilled chicken, lamb and broccoli dishes. Reservations recommended.

spots.name: Quán Ăn Ngon
spots.desc: Wide range of choices of dishes from everywhere in Vietnam at reasonable prices. Limited seating and many customers, so a wait is certain. They have a large seating area so customers do not have to wait long. Serves both lunch and dinner.

spots.name: Ramen Haron
spots.desc: Hole-in-the-wall ramen joint in Hanoi's "Japantown", frequented by Japanese expats; some staff speaks Japanese. Excellent quality and variety of ramen at very reasonable prices. Reservations recommended due to limited seating; takeaway and home deliveries also available.

spots.name: Tầm Vị
spots.desc: Vietnamese restaurant in well-preserved heritage villa, serving traditional Northern cuisine at reasonable prices. Excellent choice for first-time visitors who want authentic home-style cooking in a more upscale dining space. Inexplicably awarded a Michelin star in 2023 despite not at all being a fine dining destination, but forget about the star and you'll have a good time. To the restaurant's…

spots.name: Việt Lai Thuận
spots.desc: Grand Chinese dining hall serving the best and most authentic Sichuanese cuisine in town, alongside some Cantonese options. Caters near-exclusively to Chinese group clientele, with private rooms and karaoke facilities. Servings are all very large (sized for 3-4 pax) as a result, but kitchen can accommodate requests for half-servings.
spots.addr: 83 Hào Nam St, Chợ Dừa, Đống Đa

spots.name: dragonCELLO
spots.desc: Italian restaurant in grand colonial-style mansion, with commanding lakefront views of West Lake. Ground floor counter also offers extensive selection of Italian cured meats and cheese for takeaway. Risottos are especially good. Reservations recommended; home deliveries also available.

spots.name: Etēsia
spots.desc: Excellent contemporary European wine bar and bistro, with intimate countertop seating and dedicated cocktail bar on second floor. French head chef formerly sous chef at Michelin-starred Parisian restaurant. No tables, only 18 counter seats. Reservations recommended due to limited seating, but walk-ins also welcome.

spots.name: Gia
spots.desc: Fine dining fixed-course experience, awarded one Michelin star in 2023. Atmospheric decor and friendly, knowledgeable staff serving modern reinventions of traditional Vietnamese cuisine using local produce. Reservations essential.
spots.price: Tasting menu only: 10-course lunch from 1,800K dong, 12-course dinner from 2,590K dong

spots.name: Lamai Garden
spots.desc: Go here for a purely Vietnamese fine dining experience, without Gia's more Western-leaning influences. High-quality, farm-to-table ingredients obtained from across the north. Closed on weekends; reservations essential.
spots.price: Tasting menu only: lunch from 1,400K dong, 11-course dinner from 1,800K dong
spots.addr: 36B Đê Quai St, Tứ Liên, Tây Hồ

spots.name: JW Café
spots.desc: Luxury buffet restaurant. Immense triple-height dining room with panoramic views of adjacent lake and National Convention Center complex. Six live stations serve Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Indian, Mediterranean, BBQ, carved meat and fresh seafood selection; Sunday brunch has unlimited abalone, lobsters, French oysters and foie gras. Attached "Chocolate Lab" makes fresh, handmade truffles on site.…
spots.price: Breakfast 690K dong, lunch 590-790K dong, dinner: 1,100-1,350K dong, Sunday brunch 1,690K dong
spots.addr: 8 Đỗ Đức Dục St., Mễ Trì, Nam Từ Liêm

spots.name: LABRI Bistro
spots.desc: Out-of-the-way modern French bistro with Korean touches in casual, minimalist dining room. Excellent cooking, though portions are a tad small. Korean head chef formerly worked at Michelin-starred restaurant in Osaka. Reservations recommended.
spots.addr: 113 Bùi Thị Xuân St., Hai Bà Trưng

spots.name: Lý Club
spots.desc: Top-notch Vietnamese and European cuisine in a French colonial mansion. On the expensive side for Hanoi, but the atmosphere and good quality of food make up for it. A pianist alternates with piped music.

spots.name: Pane e Vino Italian Restaurant and Wine Shop
spots.desc: Serves a wide range of traditional regional Italian dishes. An extensive wine list with Italian wines from Veneto, Tuscany, Puglia, Sicilia, and Piedmont. Friendly service. A great place to relax and get recover after a long walking and shopping day. A/C within, extensive seating outside.

spots.name: Press Club
spots.desc: Fine dining with Western cuisine and a good selection of wines. 70-seat restaurant, private wine room for 12, and another cosy private room for 4. A combination of old and contemporary features with a classically trained chef.

spots.name: Stellar Steakhouse
spots.desc: Fine American steakhouse serving a wide range of aged meats, including authentic Japanese Kobe; named Asia's Best Luxury Steakhouse in the 2019 World Luxury Restaurant Awards. Glitzy Art Deco dining room with panoramic views of the city. Large private rooms, dedicated wine & cheese tasting room, and upstairs whisky & sake lounge. Attached mezzanine-floor Stellar Teppanyaki serves its own tasting…
spots.addr: 62nd Floor, Keangnam Hanoi Landmark Tower, Mễ Trì, Nam Từ Liêm

spots.name: Sushi Uminohana
spots.desc: Authentic omasake restaurant in Hanoi's "Japantown", serving traditional sushi, sashimi and donburi; all seafood and Wagyu beef flown fresh from Japan multiple times per week. A favourite of local Japanese expats, head chef have decade's worth of experience in Japan and speaks fluent Japanese. No tables, only 12 counter seats. Second-floor Teppan Shu exclusively serves grilled Ozaki beef.…
spots.price: Lunch donburi and omasake from 750K-1,650K dong; Dinner omasake from 1,300K-2,500K dong; Teppan Shu beef from…
spots.addr: 70 Phan Kế Bính, Cống Vị, Ba Đình

spots.name: T.U.N.G Dining
spots.desc: Hanoi's first high-end tasting menu experience. Cozy second-floor dining room, serving inventive and technically accomplished Modern Scandinavian cuisine. Reservations essential.

spots.name: Kem Tràng Tiền
spots.desc: Popular spot for ice cream on a hot day. Beware of motorbikes when entering the establishment, since it is sort of a drive-thru/drive-in ice cream shop. Recommended is the local cóm or đậu xanh flavours.

spots.name: Green Lake (Ho Guom Xanh)
spots.desc: A crowded bar with weekly performances by popular local singers. A place for the definitive Vietnamese entertainment scene. Has a cover charge on the weekends. Seems to combine part live singing with drag performances and a host club.

spots.name: Mao's Red Lounge
spots.desc: Small but lively bar with two levels, the top floor which is usually packed with Westerners smoking loads of cigarettes. Mao himself is usually in presence, playing all kinds of music from his iPod. He's extremely friendly and will strike up a conversation with anyone willing to listen.

spots.name: Minh's Jazz Club
spots.desc: This longtime institution of the Hanoi music scene is still run by the same Mr Quyen Van Minh. It seems to move venue every couple of years, so worth checking in advance. In 2015 it was in an alley behind the opera house. No cover charge, beers get more expensive (around 75,000 dong) shortly before the music starts at 21:00, but cocktails are the same price (around 100,000 dong). Offers food.

spots.name: Moon Men Cocktail Bar
spots.desc: Boutique cocktail bar on the top floor of a building with a balcony overlooking the cathedral. Menu covers homemade-infused signature cocktails as well as classics; non-alcoholic options available. Happy hour 17:00-20:00. Reservations accepted. Cash, card and QR payment.

spots.name: Standing Bar
spots.desc: Wide variety of Vietnamese craft beer, mostly from the south, but with a limited selection from the local Long Bien brewery. Despite the name, seats are available upstairs.

spots.name: Top of Hanoi
spots.desc: Large outdoor rooftop bar & brasserie with 128 seats. One of the highest bars in the world at 272 m, with commanding 360-degree views of the entire city, live DJs on Tu-Su, and open kitchen. Best visited at sunset for Golden Hour ambiance; can get quite chilly at night due to high altitude, especially during winter, so bring outerwear if necessary. Noticeably pricier than the average bar, as to…

spots.name: Highlands Coffee
spots.desc: On the 3rd floor in a ship-shaped 5-storey building (which is about to be demolished, so be quick) overlooking Hoan Kiem Lake and Vietnam's "Piccadilly Circus". Great spot to relax in scenic location where you can watch all the traffic and pedestrians go about their business below you along their outside balcony or stay inside their comfy air conditioned interior. They also serve food and beer.

spots.name: Cong Caphe
spots.desc: Several locations across the city, although the most central is probably the one at 54 Ma May. Serves various coffees, chocolates and teas including their speciality coconut coffee smoothie (around 45,000 dong). Popular with a young and relatively hip but well off crowd, and open late.

spots.name: Mien Man Cafe
spots.desc: Multi-storey art-themed cafe directly behind St. Joseph's Cathedral, serving specialty coffee and house-made syrups. Upper-floor balcony tables overlook the cathedral; non-coffee options available.

spots.name: Coconut Candy Factory
spots.desc: There are more factories around, e.g. Thanh Thanh Coconut Candies, 5km to the SE. You might get a chance to see women making the handmade candy.

spots.name: Explore the Delta
spots.desc: Boat trips are one of the nicest ways to negotiate the network of channels, but the land in between the waters is just as fascinating. It's fun to follow some of the small trails along the channels, crossing streams on very basic bridges and walking past fruit and coconut orchards.

spots.name: Ninh Kiều quán
spots.desc: Big seafood restaurant right at the beginning of town. Very popular with Vietnamese office workers and families.

spots.name: Ninh Kieu Park & Riverfront
spots.desc: Ninh Kieu Park is a city park situated along the Can Tho River, stretching from the ferry terminal at Nguyen An Ninh Rd to the Ninh Kieu Hotel at the end of Hai Ba Trung Rd. Although the park sports some greenery, one of its most noticeable features is a public square surrounding a large statue of Ho Chi Minh. The other big attraction is Ninh Kieu Tourist Market, which houses souvenir vendors…

spots.name: Can Tho Museum of Tarot
spots.desc: An unusual institution in Southeast Asia, the Museum of Tarot is a small museum with what appears to be copies of almost every tarot deck ever published, along with various other artifacts related to western esotericism, including an impressionistic portrait of Aleister Crowley.
spots.addr: 44 Đ. Nguyễn Khuyến, Tân An, Ninh Kiều

spots.name: Xuan Khanh Quarter
spots.desc: In the 18th century the quarter was named Tham Tướng after General Tham Tướng who fought the Siamese troops who were advancing from Ha Tien in 1772. The name of the place was changed after the Vietnam War to reflect the ideology of the new regime in power.

spots.name: Munirensay Temple
spots.desc: A beautiful Khmer pagoda that gives Can Tho a touch of Cambodia, recalling the region's heritage as part of the Khmer Empire.

spots.name: Chùa Ông (Ong Pagoda)
spots.desc: Just across from Ho Chi Minh's statue in Ninh Kieu Park is a little pagoda, constructed in the 1890s. Apparently a secret hideout for communist revolutionaries during the Vietnam War, the pagoda is now considered a national monument. It's worth seeing if only for its artistic value, with its intricate altars featuring carved wooden bas-reliefs.

spots.name: Quang Duc Pagoda
spots.desc: One of the biggest and most active Buddhist temples with monks living in the premises. Visitors are welcome at any time of the day. There are fewer people during the afternoon, when it is rather hot, but it gets very lively often in the evenings.

spots.name: Tin Lanh Baptist Church
spots.desc: Around 8% of Vietnamese are Catholics, but as this church demonstrates, Protestant denominations are also present.

spots.name: Canals
spots.desc: The canal system around Can Tho is a fascinating travel network, much more relaxed than the bustling roads. Hire a small rowboat (probably with a small motor as well) that can take you through the small canals that the larger tour boats cannot navigate. Tours from 06:00-14:00, including two floating markets and various sites along the canals, can be found for less than 250,000 dong per person.…

spots.name: Floating markets
spots.desc: Floating markets make for a lively scene, where many goods are exchanged, and can be easily visited by small boats for about USD3/hour per boat. You can take a tour from Ninh Kiều Pier, where the "boat ladies" are charmingly eager to welcome you aboard. Starting prices (Sep 2011) are about USD10-20 for a 3- or 7-hr tour with either one market plus canals, or several markets plus canals. It can be…

spots.name: Countryside Tour
spots.desc: If you want to go out of city, get out off the noise and enjoy natural air, the tour is designed for you. This trip provides a general view of countryside life style and packed full of fun with a lot to see, do, experience and totally worth to see. You have a chance to visit orchard islet, enjoy tropical fruits, natural wind, know how people make their living from farming and ranching, specially…

spots.name: Cái Khế Market
spots.local: Trung Tâm Thương Mại Cái Khế (Cái Khế Commercial Centre)
spots.desc: A big market catering to businesses, including restaurants and hotels, as well as end users. The market stretches over two sides of the street, with the area facing the river selling perishable foodstuffs. On the other side of the market, you will find wholesalers of textiles and home products.

spots.name: Ninh Kieu Pier Tourist Market
spots.desc: The main market of Can Tho used to be the open market on Ninh Kiều Pier. Today, the only original building left is the beautiful old market hall, now surrounded with a garden along the river. Now the Cái Khế markets further up the Can Tho River and the Xuan Khanh Market are the chief marketplaces.

spots.name: Xuan Khanh Market
spots.desc: A market predominantly for fresh food, fish, vegetables, and fruits. Other products for all daily needs are also available.

spots.name: Supermarkets
spots.desc: There are many supermarkets in Can Tho such as Coop Mart (Hoa Binh St), Metro Hung Loi (91B) (membership required), Maximark (opposite the bus station), and Vinatex Plaza in Xuan Khanh.

spots.name: Nam Bo Restaurant
spots.desc: Beautiful restaurant set in a French style villa with Hau River view from second floor, good food and so is the service.

spots.name: Nem Nuong Thanh Van
spots.desc: Famous for its "nem" or spring roll, grilled pork rolled in rice sheet with vegetable, herbs and served with dipping sauce.

spots.name: Pad Thai Tomato
spots.desc: If you don't mind eating with a predominantly foreign clientele, this place is a must try. Apart from plenty of Vietnamese dishes, there are fairly authentic dishes form Thailand, Korea, Hong Kong and Macao. The food prices are reasonable, as is the beer. Local wines are available by the glass and service is snappy and friendly.

spots.name: Gony Spa Cafe Lounge
spots.desc: Offers a variety of foods including pizza, pasta, and beefsteak as well as local food. It also offers shakes, smoothies, coffee, and ice cream.

spots.name: Hot Pot Alley
spots.desc: Hot Pot Alley is home to about a dozen restaurants all offering the same specialty, Can Tho hot pot. Hot pots are prepared DIY on a small cooker on your table. As the soup gets cooking you add different vegetables, leaves, egg or rice noodles, tofu, and eggs. You only pay for the side dishes you use and you can order more of any dish you wish. You get free refills of the hot pot soup. Ask for…

spots.name: Nam Bo
spots.desc: In a classic building facing the river, serves very tasty Vietnamese as well as some Western foods such as pizza and spaghetti. The service is nice and efficient, and a surprising variety of languages is spoken there, from English to French to Dutch and even some Japanese.

spots.name: Sao Hom
spots.desc: Serves a large palette of Vietnamese foods, and some Western food, too. The ambiance at night is special.

spots.name: International Roof Top Bar
spots.desc: Beautiful view over the city. The place is run by a young Vietnamese-German couple who moved to Can Tho from Singapore. They love music from around the world. A cosy place to relax.
spots.price: Beer USD1; spirits USD1; wine, USD1.80
spots.addr: 93 Mau Than St, Xuan Ward, Ninh Kieu

spots.name: Golf Club
spots.desc: Upscale club with many businessmen preferring this place to chill out on the weekend.

spots.name: XK club
spots.desc: Nice red-black decor with banging sound system, but quite small, therefore more secure and chill than other clubs. Pretty and friendly go-go dancers.
spots.addr: 108B Tran Van Kheo St, Ninh Kieu District

spots.name: Xe Loi Club
spots.desc: The place to be on weekends. Spacious club, good lighting/sound system with laser to boot. Most fun happens from 23:00-02:00. Youthful and energetic, but can be quite a sketchy crowd.
spots.addr: Hau Riverside Park, Bai Cat Zone, Cai Khe Ward, Ninh Kieu District

spots.name: FITO Museum of Traditional Vietnamese Medicine
spots.desc: A small museum owned by the FITO company (they produce traditional pharmaceuticals) about the history of traditional medicine in Vietnam. The rooms are filled with items ranging from ingredients to tools used to produce and prepare Vietnamese medicine. Each ticket includes an informative tour of the museum and the opportunity to sample some products. The bottom floor also has a gift shop with…

spots.name: The Geological Museum of Vietnam
spots.desc: A rare gem and a must see for geology & natural history enthusiasts. This 3-story building houses a collection of earthly artifacts (and even some non-earthly ones), including a few rare examples. Sadly in a state of neglect with poor lighting and little to no interpretive text. You can read more about it here.
spots.addr: 2 Đ. Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm, Bến Nghé, Quận 1

spots.name: Central Mosque
spots.desc: One of 12 mosques in Ho Chi Minh City, the Central Mosque was built in 1935. It was constructed for worshipers from southern India then resident in Saigon, but now Muslims from as far as Pakistan and Indonesia come to pray. Friday has the biggest congregations. The shaded veranda and cool stone floors make it an ideal place to sit, read, or even nap in the heat of the day. As with most mosques…

spots.name: Phung Son Tu Pagoda
spots.desc: Dedicated to the god of happiness and virtue. The pagoda is dusty and dwarfed by high-rises under construction nearby, but the small, sculpted grounds are a good place for a rest from the hectic city.

spots.name: Bitexco Financial Tower
spots.desc: Skydeck viewing platform (daily 09:30-21:30) with a 360° panorama of the city.
spots.price: Adult 240k VND, child (4-12) / senior (65+) / disabled 160k VND

spots.name: Dai Nam Tourist Park
spots.desc: This is one of the largest tourist attractions in Vietnam. It features the Dai Nam Van Hien Temple, an entertainment site, open range zoo, shopping areas, hotels, local and Western cuisine, and the largest man-made mountain range in Vietnam. Costing over 50 billion dong to build, this park is the beginning of mass tourism in Vietnam, although it is aimed at tourists and locals, and comes highly…
spots.price: Adult/child between 1 m and 1.4 m: zoo 80,000/50,000; amusement park 100,000/50,000 dong; waterpark 100,000/60,000…
spots.addr: Hiệp An Ward, Thủ Dầu Một city, Binh Duong

spots.name: Dam Sen Water Park
spots.desc: Close to the city centre. This water park offers some unique water slide experiences, including the amazing "Space Bowl". Restaurant, health services and animatronic dinosaurs are on the premises.
spots.price: Admission is based on height and time of arrival; under 0.8 m free, others 40-110,000 dong (90,000 after 16:00)

spots.name: Happy Ending Massage Yuan
spots.desc: Despite the name, legitimate foot and body massage, hostess will explain pricing to you at the beginning, usually offering 30% discount.
spots.addr: 15B8 Le Thanh Ton St, District 1 Ben Nighe Ward

spots.name: Twenty-Three September Park
spots.desc: Running along Phan Ngu Lao St are a number of parks which fill up with locals before sunset, after work. They play a variety of games which you can participate in: badminton, kicking a shuttlecock and women's group aerobics to music are all very popular, and are great to watch. If you sit down by yourself in the open area near the Ben Thanh market a number of young university age locals will come…

spots.name: Nguyen Hue Flower Street
spots.desc: Beautiful assortment of flowers during Tet (Lunar New Year) along the popular boulevard in District 1.

spots.name: Vietnamese Language Garden
spots.desc: The school offers one-on-one study,focus on intensive classes to get fluent in Vietnamese in a short time, or 1-2 weeks classes for tourist & homes stay to experience the local lifestyle
spots.addr: 135/10 Nguyen Cuu Van, Binh Thanh District

spots.name: Vietnamese Language Studies
spots.desc: Private school with comprehensive courses from beginner to advanced composition. Students can take private courses or join group classes.

spots.name: VNS University
spots.desc: In District 1, the University of Social Sciences has comprehensive university-style courses in Vietnamese, group classes typically 6-10 people.

spots.name: Galerie Quynh
spots.desc: A serious contemporary art gallery in District 1. Unlike the galleries that focus on more decorative works, this gallery represents innovative local and international artists including Tiffany Chung, Do Hoang Tuong, Hoang Duong Cam and Sandrine Llouquet.

spots.name: Oil-Paintings
spots.desc: There are several shops along this street selling oil paintings. If you want a portrait of a Vietnamese painting or even have your own photograph oil-painted, shop around here. You can get a portrait within a day or two.

spots.name: Tri Books
spots.desc: Stocks a wide range of English language textbooks and reference books.

spots.name: Book Street
spots.desc: Book Street has a number of book shops, both run by individual vendors and some of Vietnam’s publishing houses. You can find books in both English and Vietnamese, as well as a few other languages. Prices vary from bargain used book racks to pricy illustrated volumes hot off the press. There are two cafes on the street that are a nice stop for coffee while exploring a newly-purchased book. The…

spots.name: Ginkgo T-shirts
spots.desc: Souvenir T-shirts with creative designs inspired by Asian cultures.

spots.name: Bum Shop
spots.desc: Shop Specializes in selling unisex clothing such as loose-fit T-shirts, hoodies, jogger pants for men and women. Special sizes for foreigners.
spots.price: Tshirt 100,000 dong, Jogger Pants 180–260,000 dong, Hoodie 200,000 dong
spots.addr: 85 Tran Quoc Tuan Phuong 1 Go Vap

spots.name: Ben Thanh Market
spots.desc: A den of thieves, but great shopping for tourists — locals rarely head here for their every day needs. Ben Thanh is recognizable from its clock tower on the large roundabout. Due to its popularity with tourists, the market is now divided between tourist goods (jeans, T-shirts, smaller souvenirs in abundance) and regular items (fruit and vegetables, rice, kitchen wares, flowers, meat, fast food…

spots.name: Chợ Bình Tây
spots.desc: The underrated twin of Ben Thanh, selling everything from fruits, meat, spices, Chinese medicines, and silk to obscure varieties of fermented fish, dried seafood, and jerky. If you are searching for a variety of Vietnam silks and velvets, skip the tourist trap Ben Thanh Market and go to Bình Tây instead. Most of Chợ Bình Tây is wholesale goods. Much of Ben Thanh Market's goods are from here.

spots.name: Thái Bình Market
spots.desc: Not that large but got all the things locals need on a daily basis. Head inside the market where you can also find food stalls.

spots.name: Night Market
spots.desc: Here you can enjoy many kinds of different foods and drink and do your shopping as well. But it is just a small street with traffic passing and pushy sellers, not the nicest place to hang around.

spots.name: Saigon Square
spots.desc: A good place for a visit. It is a twin of Ben Thanh but with air conditioning. Haggling your way through this place is the rule of thumb. Local middle-class Vietnamese shop here on the weekends too. Consider planning your shopping here during the day and go to Ben Thanh for the night market. The daytime Ben Thanh can be planned as a sightseeing trip instead of a shopping spree.

spots.name: War Surplus Market
spots.desc: Sometimes called the American Market or "Cho Cu" or "Khu Dan Sinh". Hidden behind rows of hardware and electric supplies shops, just brace yourself and enter. Dense warrens of stalls include those selling old American military gear of indeterminate authenticity (e.g., "nice collection of so-called authentic GI's Zippo lighter from the war era"), cheap T-shirts and military paraphernalia: just…

spots.name: Bách Hóa XANH
spots.desc: A inexpensive supermarket in the center with evening specials of fruits, meat and fish.

spots.name: Co-op Mart Supermarkets
spots.desc: Co-op Mart can be found everywhere around HCMC. Prices are reasonably lower, though the selection leans more toward Vietnamese foods. 32 stores in Ho Chi Minh City.

spots.name: Giant Supermarket
spots.desc: Part of dairy farm Hong Kong which has supermarkets all over Asia.

spots.name: ÆON Mall Binh Tan
spots.desc: In Binh Tan district, a large shopping mall with the food hall where you can get some Japanese food.

spots.name: ÆON Mall Tan Phu Celadon
spots.desc: The first branch of Japanese retail chain Aeon in Ho Chi Minh City.

spots.name: CGV Giga Mall Thủ Đức
spots.desc: In Thu Duc district, a large shopping mall with numerous options to keep the kids occupied.

spots.name: CGV Vincom Center Landmark 81
spots.desc: Located at the bottom of the tallest building in Vietnam, with numerous mid tier luxury brands

spots.name: Crescent Mall
spots.desc: In District 7, a large shopping centre primarily filled with mid-ranged international brands. Also home to a gaming stadium where you can watch some e-sports.

spots.name: Diamond Plaza
spots.desc: A department store behind Notre Dame Cathedral, across the street diagonally.

spots.name: Saigon Center
spots.desc: A mall near Ben Thanh Market, just across the street from Saigon Square. Look for the Takashimaya sign. Many high-end luxury brands have branches here.

spots.name: SC VivoCity
spots.desc: In District 7, a large shopping centre with a rooftop garden and a playground to keep children occupied.

spots.name: Ben Thanh Market
spots.desc: It's a rather touristy market where you still can enjoy the most authentic Vietnamese pho.

spots.name: Bánh Mì 37
spots.desc: Absolutely delicious even though a bit different than the traditional. Popular among locals, there might be a queue.

spots.name: Pho 24
spots.desc: Clean modern chain found everywhere in Ho Chi Minh City. Excellent beef noodle soup, very cheap. Watch out for the fake Pho 24/24 on Pham Ngu Lao St, which does not belong to the chain and serves terrible and expensive food.

spots.name: Pho Quynh
spots.desc: Their specialty is pho. Locals come regularly and lucky backpackers stumble upon it. It is air-conditioned on the second and third floors. They also have decent banh mi bo kho, which is beef stew with carrots, served with French baguette.

spots.name: Nhà Hàng Chay Ngọc Thọ
spots.desc: Incredible range of delicoius veggie options, but also meat and chicken. Clean place, friendly staff, tasty food and satisfying portions.

spots.name: Nhà Hàng Asian Kitchen
spots.desc: Very good place for delicious and diverse food, big choice. Kinda hidden, kinda great. Also lots of vegetarian options.

spots.name: Bánh Mì Hồng Hoa
spots.desc: Banh Mi with local taste. Fresh bread (Vietnamese baguette) with various choices.

spots.name: Bún Chả 145
spots.desc: Typical restaurant in the most amazing street of the city. Very good place for Bun Cha. As of February 2026, it is closed for renovation.

spots.name: The Lunch Lady
spots.desc: The famous Lunch Lady was featured on Anthony Bourdain's show. Different noodle dish every day.

spots.name: Barbecue Garden
spots.desc: A barbecue restaurant offering both Vietnamese and international foods.

spots.name: Bi Saigon
spots.desc: Extensive menu with a choice between Vietnamese, Italian, Mexican and other styles. Open plan kitchen so you can see your food being prepared.

spots.name: Hoa Khai Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.desc: Tasty Vietnamese vegetarian food although with surly service. Be careful of being charged for unexpected items, such as the disposable hand towels that are presented to you without asking as you sit down.
spots.addr: 124 126 Nguyen Cu Trinh St, Cu Trinh Ward, District 1

spots.name: Hủ Tiếu Hồng Phát
spots.desc: Restaurant selling Hủ tiếu Nam Vang, a flat rice noodle dish that is a specialty of the city. The dish is often called "Cambodian noodles" in English, even though it cannot be found in Cambodia.

spots.name: Quan An Ngon
spots.desc: Two different restaurants operate with the same name within a few blocks of each other, one at 160 Pasteur Street, and the other on Nam Ky Khoi Nghia across from the Reunification Palace. Set in atmospheric old French villas, with similar menus Vietnamese food, including regional specialities prepared in numerous independently-operated food stalls around the perimeter. Both are popular and both…

spots.name: Bloom Saigon Restaurant
spots.desc: Temporarily closed as of August 2022. Non-profit restaurant run by Aid to Children Without Parents (ACWP) and serves as a culinary training facility. Very nice staff, excellent food, terrace on the 3rd floor. Situated a bit in the North and in a small calm community. Worth to go by foot, 20 mnin walk from the Jade Pagoda.
spots.addr: 3/5 Hoàng Sa, P. Đa Kao, Quận 1

spots.name: Au Lac do Brazil
spots.desc: Just to prove that Saigon has everything, here is a Brazilian-style churrascaria (all-you-can-eat restaurant featuring barbecued meat), with live Latin music Tuesday to Saturday. They also have a new outlet in Sky Garden II, Phu My Hung, District 7. It's a larger and less crowded one with usually better service.

spots.name: The Deck Saigon
spots.desc: The only posh restaurant on the banks of the river. Modern fusion cuisine using the local ingredients.
spots.addr: 38 Nguyen U Di, Thao Dien, An Phu, District 2

spots.name: Anan Saigon
spots.desc: A premier fine dining restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City, one of only two in Vietnam to be ranked among Asia's top 50 restaurants. Reservations essential.
spots.addr: 89 Tôn Thất Đạm, Bến Nghé, District 1

spots.name: Halal@Saigon
spots.desc: Vietnamese, Malaysian, and vegetarian cuisine prepared to halal guidelines. Has a Malaysian owner and there are several Malaysian staples on the menu, however it is primarily Vietnamese, with a wide range of dishes from around the country.

spots.name: Bobby Brewery Coffee
spots.desc: Nice place with good beverages. Used to show movies on 2nd and 3rd floor. Now reopened as La Cantina.

spots.name: Cafe Napoly
spots.desc: The decor is Roman ruins-lite (they meant "Napoli"), but the menu is typical for an upscale Vietnamese cafe: coffee, fruit drinks, ice cream, and a simple menu including eggs and rice dishes. Piped music is nice, not too loud by day (though louder at night), prices are decent. Outdoor terrace in the front, air-con section on the ground floor, and evening lounge-bar on the upper floor. Next door…

spots.name: Chao Ba Ca Phe
spots.desc: This place has a really authentic and wonderful cafe sua da served by the famous "grandma" for about 8,000 dong. A little tricky to find.

spots.name: Givral Café
spots.desc: In the French tradition, with fresh pastries, collared waiters and elaborate portions of ice cream. Well-located, but over 20,000 dong for the simplest cup.

spots.name: Hideaway Café
spots.desc: As its name implies, this place is hidden away and a good place to read, or have a quiet conversation or meal. Decent Western menu, although slightly pricey.

spots.name: Highlands Coffee
spots.desc: Highlands Coffee is a Vietnamese chain that is ubiquitous in Ho Chi Minh City. They offer a variety of coffee drinks reasonably priced (25,000-60,000 dong, depending on your order) with consistent quality.

spots.name: M-Comic
spots.desc: A rather hard to find coffee shop. Upstairs is like a bedroom with a couple of beds. Arrive early if you want to occupy one. It has a large selection of magazine and comic books to choose from. Only serves Vietnamese drinks, and the staff only speak a little English. Free Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Old Saigon Coffee
spots.desc: Reminiscent of HCMC in the past. It has a great view of Dong Khoi St. All the drinks and foods are typical Saigon. The staff are quite decent.

spots.name: Regina Coffee
spots.desc: Vietnamese coffee or cappuccini. They have a skilled Japanese espresso master who knows how to brew coffee. French mixed with Asian design with brick walls. It is marketed towards tourists and all proceeds go to the church around the corner.

spots.name: Trung Nguyen
spots.desc: The Vietnamese version of Starbucks, but with much better coffee. They have locations all over the city, but are not well represented in the heart of the tourist district. Prices start around 40,000 dong for a basic cuppa, although there are plenty of variations including the infamous weasel coffee (cà phê chồn), made from coffee beans collected from civet excrement; however, a quick Google…

spots.name: Chill Sky Bar
spots.desc: Rooftop bar at AB Tower in District 1 along September 23 park. This is the place to see and to be seen. Drinks are expensive at 200,000 dong and up. If you are around the September 23 park at night you will see the lights and hear the music blasting from the top of the AB tower. Look for the spotlights shooting into the sky.

spots.name: Acoustic Cafe
spots.desc: Though only 1 km from the heavily touristed centre, this club is completely outside the tourist orbit, and offers an interesting view of local life. The all-Vietnamese house band performs every night, mostly American music, and it's always jammed with student-aged groupies. For some reason, they address the crowd in English between songs, even though half the crowd doesn't understand. On…

spots.name: Banana Pub
spots.desc: Park View. Pool table, darts, friendly staff, beautiful people, loads of food. Stays open late depending on the crowd. Worth a trip from Q1 to experience the expat scene.

spots.name: Carmen
spots.desc: The house band has changed some personnel but is still good, specializing in flamenco, salsa and Latin pop, and with an eclectic mix of other popular songs thrown in. Cocktails 110,000 dong, shots 80-85,000 dong, but with no entrance charge. It's popular and fills up on weekends.

spots.name: Ice Blue
spots.desc: Centrally located English pub, complete with darts board and warm beer. Friendly, but shuts at midnight.

spots.name: Khong Ten
spots.desc: Large cabaret featuring some of the biggest Vietnamese celebrity singers in Vietnam. The headliner is often familiar to the locals from television. Most overseas visitors may not like the musical style as it is mostly the mellow-to-melancholy, soft-jazzy, love-ballady style favoured by the middle and older generation of Vietnamese. But it's pure Vietnam, and very popular with both HCMC residents…

spots.name: Lion's
spots.desc: Brewery, restaurant offering German food, with tasty beers and cocktails. The outside terrace is a nice place to chill out, and the inside restaurant is very welcoming with its two beer tanks and cosy bar.

spots.name: Lush
spots.desc: A nightclub in the Western style, with loud music and minimalist too-cool decor. Drink prices on par with most Saigon nightclubs. Mixed crowd (Vietnamese, tourists and expats), pretty good food but has a small dance floor. Ladies night on Tuesday offers free drinks for ladies until midnight. Be sure to arrive early as it gets very busy from around 22:30 and it is difficult to get served at the…

spots.name: Metallic Bar
spots.desc: House band plays covers of Metallica, Guns 'n Roses and other popular rock bands nightly between 21:00 and midnight.

spots.name: Peaches
spots.desc: Great place to enjoy a few drinks with friends. Friendly staff, Asian food. Quite low key in comparison to other PMH bars.

spots.name: Polo
spots.desc: Mixture of expats and locals, starts getting busy quite early. Music from the 1980s to the present. Noisy and smokey.

spots.name: Q Bar Saigon
spots.desc: Established in 1992 under the Opera House. Mix of locals, tourists and expats in a grotto-like uber-chic setting that could as easily be in Soho as Saigon. Open till late every night. Great cocktails, though at very high prices, similar to the roof-top bar of the Caravelle Hotel across the street. It's the cool place to be seen if you have a lot of Uncle Hos in your pocket. Terrace and Indoor…

spots.name: Rio Saigon
spots.desc: A Brazilian flowery decor-themed bar/pub with a Filipino house band playing pop/rock such as Bon Jovi and Skid Row.

spots.name: Saigon Pho
spots.desc: This little hole in the wall is only a stone's throw from Allez Boo, but much more expat orientated. Open until late.

spots.name: Serenata and Soi Da
spots.desc: Two open-air cafe-bars with live music in villa-style settings, which attract few if any tourists but typify what most Vietnamese consider a pleasant evening out. Both feature a mix of classical chamber music, Vietnamese lounge songs, American FM classics and the odd French song.

spots.name: Velvet
spots.desc: Nice ambiance & music. Latest chic bar in town. Gets very busy, and at weekends you will need a booking.

spots.name: Alibi
