spots.desc: Very cosy atmosphere, with sofas lining the walls and beautiful decor. Good food & drinks selection, nice music, and a mix of both locals & expats. Friendly staff, and the management's always there to make you feel welcome and make sure you get what you are asking for.

spots.name: Allez Boo
spots.desc: For those who have been here before, you'll find the original bar is now Highlands Coffee and an all new Allez Boo has opened on the opposite corner. It's shiny and brand-new, but retains the same feel as the original. There's a bar with air-con on the 2nd floor with DJ-type music, and an airy rooftop patio. Quite similar to its sibling establishment, Go2 Bar.

spots.name: Apocalypse Now
spots.desc: Legendary and still packed on weekends, although aside from a few movie references it's not all that much to look at. Stays open late. Now opened their 2nd floor for DJ, dancing, drinks with less crowded atmosphere.

spots.name: Catwalk
spots.desc: All-in-one place with a massage parlour, disco, KTV, and a mini-casino. Price is on the expensive side, but it is a sight to behold.

spots.name: Go2 Bar
spots.desc: The main backpacker bar while Allez Boo was closed, still a great meeting place. It's impossible to miss the four floors of neon lights on the outside. Large patio on the sidewalk at street level, a cosier bar on the second floor with occasional live music or big-screen sports, plus a rooftop patio (with retractable roof) with individual BBQs up a steep set of stairs on the 5th floor.

spots.name: Oblivion
spots.desc: Late night venue with lots of character, claims to be Saigon's premier music bar and it's hard to argue, assuming, that is, you have a taste for non-chart buzzy British guitar and obscure dark US/European stuff. You have to ask for happy pop, though if you're spending enough it'll sometimes get an outing. Like most Saigon bars, it attracts its share of working girls. If you're not interested…

spots.name: Pasteur Street Brewing Company
spots.desc: A cozy bar that specializes in craft beer microbrews. A large selection of their own beers that run between 50,000-300,000 dong per glass (though most are 105,000 for a regular size). They also serve food and bar snacks. Mostly expats and tourists with a laid back yet classy atmosphere. The original tap rooms are down an alley off Pasteur Street, but there are clearly marked signs to guide you…
spots.addr: 144 Pasteur, Bến Nghé, District 1 (this is the original location, but others can be found throughout the city)

spots.name: 163 Cyclo Bar
spots.desc: Two doors down from the Duna Hotel. Thumping music until 02:00 with friendly staff. Sex workers catering to Western men here. If you're not interested, just gently let it be known.

spots.name: Le Pub
spots.desc: Always busy after 18:00, famous for its strong drinks, daily dollar-specials (e.g., Tuesday USD1 for vodka mixers all night) and friendly staff. It has the same owner as Le Pub in Hanoi. The Pub Quiz (almost every Tuesday) is very popular with expats, especially the English teachers. Get there early or it's too packed to find a place to sit down. Indoors and outdoor tables available.

spots.name: Rex Hotel Rooftop
spots.desc: They serve a buffet dinner at the dinner hour, which gradually gives way to drinks and music. Acts change over time, but have included a Filipino band playing FM classics and a Vietnamese group playing Latin and flamenco. It's a pleasant place to get above the city noise and enjoy some fresh air. Cocktails around 140,000 dong.

spots.name: Saigon Saigon
spots.desc: A pleasant, breezy bar with a great view of the city. Great live band (Cuban) playing inside every night. Cool, quiet ambience on the terrace. Attracts an expense-account crowd due to the prices.

spots.name: Seventeen Saloon
spots.desc: American Wild West-themed bar, live music every night and other entertainment. Drinks are expensive.

spots.name: Sheridan's
spots.desc: Small, cosy Irish-themed bar with imported draft beer and live music. Brits will appreciate the great food tasting of home (or the closest you'll get here).

spots.name: Vasco's
spots.desc: Live music on some nights of the week and a typical bar atmosphere for tourists and expats. Drinks from 50,000 dong, including sales tax, tip not necessary.

spots.name: VIBE Billiards & Lounge
spots.desc: Professional billiards tables and a spacious lounge. Food and drinks and you can customise the billiard table lights from a special lighting system.
spots.addr: 02 Sương Nguyệt Ánh, Phường Bến Thành, Quận 1

spots.name: ZanZBar
spots.desc: Casual-upscale, the clients tend to come for the great choice of wines-by-the-glass (huge walk-in wine cellar), or for the cocktails (premium brands) and good selection of imported beers. Can remain open after midnight, depending on the number of customers.

spots.name: Binh Son sea park
spots.desc: A spacious coastal area where visitors can swim, stroll, and take photos among the lawns, flower gardens, and stone-paved walkways.

spots.name: Chu Ngo Chicken Rice
spots.desc: Serves chicken rice, pork rice, chicken pho and other dishes.

spots.name: Central Market
spots.desc: The busiest market in Phan Thiet with various food and clothing stalls. Expect to do lots of haggling. More than anything, the markets are known for their fresh seafood.

spots.name: Bách Hóa XANH
spots.desc: The supermarket popular for its daily fruit and evening meat and fish specials and in general not as expensive as Coop or Lotte.

spots.name: Lotte Mart
spots.desc: A big mall from Lotte, a corporation from Korea. It is in the heart of the city, Phú Thủy. It has a shopping mall, clothes shops and restaurants.
spots.addr: Hùng Vương I residential area, Phú Thủy Ward

spots.name: Coop Mart
spots.desc: A large, Western-style grocery store that also sells books, jewellery and necessities.

spots.name: Mom's Bun Dau 62 pieces
spots.desc: They serve a mixed meat platter which is very popular with the locals and comes at an incredible price. You enjoy it just with strong fish sauce or roll the available pieces and salad into rice paper and dip it into sweet, salty sauce. (Use the cucumber pieces to make the rice paper moist a little, so it can be rolled better.).

spots.name: Sunworld Cable Car
spots.desc: A 30-min cable car trip takes you 7.9 km over several island and pearl fishing farms to the Sunworld Hon Thom Water Park. Beautiful views.

spots.name: Sao Beach
spots.desc: The prettiest beach on the island, with a restaurant/cafe and beach lounging.

spots.name: Ong Lang Beach
spots.desc: Beautiful beach to watch the sunset. Most of it is managed and cleaned by some resorts, but you can lie on the sand with your towel no questions asked, or go to the partially rocky part on the north end, away from the resorts.

spots.name: Suoi Tranh Waterfalls
spots.desc: This is a major attraction when it has been raining. There is barely any water during the dry season from Nov-Apr, but the rock exposed by the river is interesting, and you can hear the sounds of the forest. You can plunge into the pool under the 2-m waterfall at the end of the path.

spots.name: Phu Quoc Prison History Museum
spots.desc: Historical prison built by French and used during Vietnam War for POW.

spots.name: Sunworld Hon Thom Water Park
spots.desc: A modern water theme park (opened in 2019) with massive water slides, swimming pools restaurants, and a beach offer snorkeling and scuba diving. A free buggy takes you from the cable car to the beach (turn right after you exit the cable car).

spots.name: Jerry's Jungle Tours
spots.desc: Archipelago explorations by boat, snorkelling, fishing, day and multiday trips to islands, motorbike tours, bouldering, bird-watching, hiking and cultural tours around Phu Quoc.

spots.name: Flipper Diving Club
spots.desc: The only dive company on Phú Quôc that is a PADI resort and also a SSI center. Staffed by instructors from both organizations, they can provide training from beginner level to all the way up to divemaster. They are also environmentally aware and organize clean up days, actively try to raise awareness of divers and enforce a "no-touch" policy while diving.
spots.price: Fun Dives US$65, for non-certified divers starting from USD85, PADI & SSI courses starting from US$300

spots.name: Vietnam explorers
spots.desc: Formerly Rainbow Divers (as evidenced by the inherited marketing text and the recommendation by Rainbow Divers Nha Trang). The longest established dive centre on Phú Quôc. PADI-courses, snorkelling and diving are available in most European languages and in Vietnamese. Friendly staff and great and safe trips.
spots.addr: DT 47 Group 2, Suoi May Hamet, Duong To Commune, Phu Quoc

spots.name: X-Dive
spots.desc: Operates dives to the north and south of the island depending upon the conditions. They do not offer PADI courses.

spots.name: Phú Quôc Island Tours
spots.desc: English & Vietnamese tour guides taking you to the island hotspots by land and sea. Services include camping, kayak+camping, and National Park trekking.
spots.addr: 1 Tran Hung Dao Street (near the Salinda Resort)

spots.name: Dinh Cau Night Market
spots.desc: Later, try wandering around the night market where locals mingle with tourists, a place that offers a selection of goods, pearls, seafood, and a playground for children. There are many options for food at the market, with fresh seafood laid out next to each restaurant for you to check out while you're making your choice of place to sit and eat.

spots.name: The Dog Bar
spots.desc: Serves good burgers and pizzas, as well as a range of Western, Vietnamese, and seafood dishes. Watch live sports, play pool, or darts, or just listen to live music. You can book dive and snorkelling trips there with Rainbow Divers and Anh Tu. They have cold beer, mixed drinks and cocktails and a friendly English-speaking staff.
spots.addr: 88 Tran Hung Dao, Dương Đông town

spots.name: Ganesh Indian Restaurant
spots.desc: The food is OK, but not quite up to the standards you can experience in countries like the UK or Australia.
spots.addr: 97 Tran Hung Dao, Dương Đông town

spots.name: Gio Bien Restaurant
spots.desc: Offers a great selection of fresh seafood dishes and Vietnamese dishes. The beach is beautiful and metres away from your table. The caramelised fish hotpot for lunch or dinner is a treat.

spots.name: Night Market
spots.desc: From 18:00 there are lots of small restaurants open on the street of the night market. It's the place to go for seafood.
spots.addr: Võ Thị Sáu, Dương Đông town

spots.name: Ocean Bar and Grill
spots.desc: Excellent service and food. The seafood is fresh and cooked to order and the staff are highly trained and attentive. Michelle, the owner, speaks to every customer about their meal and keeps a photo and book of comments from all patrons.

spots.name: Rory's Beach Bar
spots.desc: As you walk past on the beach the Aussie owner, Rory, will tempt you with promises of ice cold beer ("Too cold to hold!") using his loud hailer. He delivers, with two draught beers on tap. There's plenty of room to sit and relax on the deck, around the bar or on the beach-front. Prices are mid-range with draught beer around 35,000 dong, cocktails hovering around 100,000 dong and meals averaging…

spots.name: The Rabbit Hole Irish Sports Bar
spots.desc: English-speaking staff, outdoor seating, air-conditioned indoors and free wifi. Western and Vietnamese specialties. A selection of big screens showing sports, pool table, a Professional UK darts board, regular poker games, a NES Classic with 30 classic games, Jenga, and Connect 4. Also serving Guinness, Magners’ Cider and many more Western and local beers, fine whiskeys and signature cocktails.
spots.addr: 118/2/1 Đường Trần Hưng Đạo, Khu Phố 7

spots.name: Bạch Dinh
spots.desc: Built by the French (1898-1916) as a summer holiday house for French Governor-General Paul Doumer. Also formerly known as Dinh Toàn Quyền (Villa du Gouverneur). Under French rule, the mansion was a holiday getaway for French governors and Bảo Đại, the last Emperor of Vietnam. During the American War, the mansion was used for R&R. Since the end of the American War, the mansion has been for public…

spots.name: Đài Liệt Sĩ
spots.desc: A stone obelisk on a hilltop, on the way to the sea, the Soldiers' Memorial Hill is said to incorporate the biggest traffic circle in Indochina. A cool hangout for lovers.

spots.name: Đình Thần Thắng Tam
spots.local: Thắng Tam Local Gods Communal House
spots.desc: According to legend, it was built in the Minh Mạng dynasty (1820-1840) as a place to worship the 3 men who set up the 3 villages of Thắng in Vũng Tàu, starting a new way of life. The architecture is particularly interesting around the Tam Quan Gate, the sanctum, the public commune, the meeting room, and the stage for military operas that is skillfully engraved. The sanctum is roofed with…

spots.name: Pagodas
spots.desc: Niết Bàn Tịnh Xá and Thích Ca Phật Đài are most popular among the pagodas and temples in Vũng Tàu.

spots.name: Robert Taylor Museum of Worldwide Arms
spots.desc: A fascinating collection of arms and uniforms from around the world. Most major wars and battles are covered. The emphasis is in British and Australian regimental uniforms but there are also Samurai, Mongols, Saracens, Turks and Bulgarians as well as most European and North American armies. There is a wide range of guns, swords and other weapons of war. Quite why Bob Taylor chose to open his…

spots.name: Ho May Park
spots.desc: Fun day out if you have kids (quite fun even if you don't!). Dodgems, Go-Karts, various fairground rides, a large water park, a games centre, the 'Alpine Luge' and other attractions are all included in the cost!
spots.addr: 1A Trần Phú, Phường 1, Vũng Tàu, Bà Rịa

spots.name: Bãi Sau
spots.desc: Also known as Thùy Vân Beach. The only standard beach for tourism in Vung Tau. It is 3 km long and stretches from the Small Mount to Paradise Park. All beaches here are free. You must pass through some "water parks" to get to the beach in some places, in most places there is a pleasant promenade that leads directly to the beach. The beach is clean, the water is shallow quite a way out, there are…
spots.price: Locker 15,000 dong, beach umbrella 30,000 dong, chaise longue 25,000 dong, deck chair and umbrella 50,000 dong, fresh…

spots.name: Long Hải
spots.desc: A nearby seaside town. The beach here is smaller, but the town owns a local goddess temple called "Dinh Cô" which holds an annual cultural festival called "Dinh Cô Festival". It is one of the three well-known traditional festivals in southern Vietnam. The town also features Minh Đạm Tunnel, a former hideout of the Viet Minh during the wars.

spots.name: Long Sơn
spots.desc: Head here for the wooden Nhà Lớn Long Sơn complex dating from the 19th century.

spots.name: Vũng Tàu Market
spots.desc: The central market built in 1985. Vietnamese day meals start with market. Goods in markets are cheaper and fresher than in shops and that's why a market is very familiar with every Vietnamese, esp. housewives.

spots.name: Lottle Mall Vung Tau
spots.desc: A mall from the corporation Lotte from South Korea, it is to the right of the Bãi sau. It has a shopping mall (includes household stuff), restaurants, clothes shops.
spots.addr: At the corner of road Thi Sách & road 3/2, Ward No.8

spots.name: Bò Kho
spots.desc: Delicious Vietnamese goulash (Bò Kho) served with a Bánh mì and salad.

spots.name: Sủi Cảo
spots.desc: They call it Sủi Cảo, but it is similar to, if not the same as Hoành Thánh Mỳ, i.e. Wonton dumplings, served in Hoi An. 4 dumplings prepared in soup or deep-fried.

spots.name: Quan Su Bin - Bò Lá Lốt
spots.desc: Grilled minced beef rolled into wine leaves. You take that and vegetables, roll them into rice paper and dip them into sweet and salt sauce for final consumption. The owner ladies are not particularly friendly, but don't let spoil you meal.

spots.name: Loan Cháo Lòng
spots.desc: Intestines porridge, for people how like experimenting and to experience the full range of Vietnamese cuisine.

spots.name: Bistro Nine
spots.desc: Bistro style, open early for breakfast until late for dinner. Large wine cellar, bakery, house-made excellent bread and charcuterie. Nice place to chill out for coffee or dinner. Sandwiches, wood oven pizzas, meats, fish, great ribs.

spots.name: David Pizzeria
spots.desc: An Italian restaurant with a wide selection of pasta, wood-fired pizza, seafood, wine, and Italian desserts. They also have fresh bread, coffees. Delivery available.

spots.name: Nhà hàng Kozak
spots.desc: Ukrainian restaurant, decorated with Ukrainian stuff. Restaurant offers traditional beverages: Ukrainian liquors, borsht, vareniki, kvass.

spots.name: Vườn Bàng
spots.desc: Large indoor restaurant, ideal place for parties. Special foods include shashlyk (Russian fried pork) and Russian salad.

spots.name: Matilda's Pub
spots.desc: Laidback Aussie pub. The cheapest beers/drinks in town. Very affordable meals, including breakfast. Happy hour every day from 09:00-18:00. Very friendly staff. An excellent place to enjoy a relaxing beer or meal.

spots.name: Mr Splash Cocktail Bar
spots.desc: Makes amazing coffee, tea and cocktails at very affordable prices. Very professional, and Phú is a proper bartender.

spots.name: Bistro Nine
spots.desc: Espresso, cappuccino, fresh juice and home made French ice cream. Indoor-outdoor.

spots.name: Belly's Restaurant and Watering Hole
spots.desc: Belly's is a super friendly Aussie pub that also serves excellent food. Relax with a game of pool, watch the footy or chat with the regulars. Great, friendly and efficient staff.

spots.name: Cafe Rin
spots.desc: Serves a decent cup of strong, dark, and rich aromatic coffee. Said to serve only coffees that are grown directly from Vietnam highland provinces. The beans here are kept fresh and are ground only on order. Popular for to go orders among locals and tourists alike.

spots.name: Lotte Mart shopping centre
spots.desc: Large shopping complex with a cinema on the top level.

spots.name: Hải sản Mộc quán
spots.desc: Seafood. Busy and crowded with locals.

spots.name: Happy Heart Cafe
spots.desc: Tasty food, friendly people.
spots.addr: 57 Đ. Ng. Thì Sĩ, Bắc Mỹ An

spots.name: Torino Restaurant & Bakery
spots.desc: Italian food. The pizza dough is excellent.

spots.name: Limoncello
spots.desc: Great Italian food with homemade limoncello.

spots.name: Ngoi Café
spots.desc: A inexpensive and comfortable little café.

spots.name: Tuy Anh Chinese Chess Coffee Shop
spots.desc: Hangout for coffee-drinking Chinese chess enthusiasts.

spots.name: Cam Pho Communal House
spots.addr: 52 Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai, Phường Minh An

spots.name: Phuc Kien Meeting Hall
spots.desc: Hokien (Fujian) meeting hall built in 1757.

spots.name: Hai Nam Assembly Hall
spots.desc: Hainanese community meeting hall built in 1875.

spots.name: Hoi An Traditional Art Performance House
Morning Market
spots.desc: Produce, fish, and meat at local prices.

spots.name: Quán Mười
spots.desc: Besides Mì Quảng, they also serve delicious Cao lầu.

spots.name: Thành Nam Quán
spots.desc: Tiny Vietnamese restaurant where everything is delicious.
spots.price: Plates from 50,000 dong, mains from 80,000 dong

spots.name: Nguyen Van Cu Bookstore
spots.addr: By the Dong Hoi Citadel Gates

spots.name: Nhu Y
spots.desc: Good Vietnamese food. They have English menu.

spots.name: Bar Hoang De
spots.desc: Discotheque, cocktails, beer, coffee, fruit shakes.

spots.name: Coco's Coffee Bar Classic
spots.desc: Free Wi-Fi, coffee, fruit juices, breakfast.

spots.name: Banh Bao
spots.desc: A street vendor who sells wonderful Banh Bao.

spots.name: Cơm Chay Diệu Lạc
spots.desc: Simple and good vegetarian meals.

spots.name: Ta.ke Japanese Restaurant
spots.desc: Excellent food.

spots.name: Café on Thu Wheels
spots.desc: It's a little bar owned by the charming lady Thu.

spots.name: roller blading
spots.desc: On the 2nd floor of the Nha Trang Centre, shopping mall.

spots.name: Surfing Shack
spots.desc: Bar, restaurant and surf club/school.

spots.name: Shop Herman
spots.desc: Clothes from back home at half the cost.

spots.name: VinCom Plaza
spots.desc: Large Western-style supermarket.

spots.name: Mê Linh 68 - Bánh Hỏi
spots.desc: Authentic and inexpensive Bánh Hỏi.

spots.name: Roasted Duck Shop 69
spots.desc: Delicious noodles and roasted duck.

spots.name: Ẩm Thực Chay - Bồ Đề Sao
spots.desc: Great place for vegetarian dishes.

spots.name: Phở Bò Hà Nội
spots.desc: Delicious pho and known for their dishes with rice noodles.

spots.name: Cheers Sports Pub
spots.desc: Western home style food and big TVs to watch sport events.

spots.name: Crazy Kim Bar
spots.desc: If you are young and wild, this is the place to be.

spots.name: Ho Chi Minh Square
spots.desc: Has a statue of Ho Chi Minh and a fountain.

spots.name: Chợ Ga Vinh
spots.desc: It has various stalls.

spots.name: Golden Spring Lake
spots.desc: Unspoiled scenery.

spots.name: Sữa đậu nành Nguyễn Văn Cừ -Soya Milk Stall
Quán Cơm chay An Lạc Tâm
IndiaGate
spots.desc: Indian restaurant. Vegan and halal options available.

spots.name: Fungi Chingu Chợ Đêm - Quán nướng Hàn Quốc

spots.desc: Medium-sized Buddhist temple a 4-min walk from Coopmart just west of Nguyễn Tất Thành Street.

spots.name: Chùa Long Khánh
spots.desc: Large and very important Buddhist temple in Quy Nhơn city and Bình Định province. The temple was first constructed in the early 1700s, but nothing of the original structure remains. The current main building was erected in 1956, and the Buddha statue and lotus pond were completed in 1972. The 1.7 m (5.6 ft) high, 700 kg (1,500 lb) bell was believed to have been cast in 1805. Inside is a statue of…

spots.name: Chùa Minh Tịnh
spots.desc: Large and active Mahayana Buddhist pagoda complex in the city centre a 10-minute walk west of Coopmart. Founded in 1917 outside the city, it was moved in the 1960s to its current location to make room for the expansion of the airport during the Vietnam-American war. The well-maintained temple, which is surrounded by spacious and peaceful grounds with many colourful statues, is an active and…

spots.name: Chùa Phổ Minh
spots.desc: Impressive and little-visited Buddhist temple of 800 m² (8,600 ft²) set on tranquil riverside grounds of 1,800 m² (19,000 ft²). Work began on the site in 2011. Soon after, five workers were gravely injured in a major accident when the concrete and steel of the third floor collapsed. Construction was suspended, but with the prayers of the monks and the enthusiastic support of the injured workers…

spots.name: Chùa Tâm Ấn Tự
spots.desc: Active Mahayana Buddhist temple on a tranquil 2,000 m² (21,000 ft²) site. A small hut on the grounds began serving as a spiritual home for monks in the 1920s but was destroyed during war activities in the 1940s. The temple was restarted under new spiritual advisers in 1955, and the structure was built out very, very slowly. After 40 years of glacial progress, construction on the current temple…

spots.name: Chùa Tịnh xá Ngọc Nhơn
spots.desc: Buddhist temple in the northwest of the city. Nestled amidst the trees and set back against the mountain, the temple's 2,500 m² (27,000 ft²) grounds are a surprisingly peaceful contrast to the bustle of the heavily trafficked street outside. It was built in 1959 and was restored from 1995 to 1999. Open to visitors daily from morning to evening.

spots.name: Chùa Trúc Lâm
spots.desc: Well-maintained six-storey Buddhist temple in the northern end of the city centre. Open to visitors daily from morning to evening.

spots.name: Tượng Phật đôi
spots.desc: Towering above the ocean on the Phương Mai Peninsula, this 30-m (100-ft) golden Avalokiteśvara, the embodiment of infinite compassion of all Buddhas, is the tallest Buddha statue in Vietnam. Constructed in 2014, the base is designed to hold the ashes of 8,000 local families.

spots.name: Bình Định Museum
spots.desc: Located in the east of the centre near the Municipal People's Administrative buildings, this small building has a large collection of Cham artefacts making it more interesting than you'd expect for a small provincial museum. The museum's Cham collection has grown significantly over the last two decades as new expeditions jointly conducted with Belgian and Japanese archaeological teams and Polish…

spots.name: Municipal People's Government Offices
spots.desc: Imposing and stern complex of several multi-storey buildings housing the city-government offices built in classic communist architectural style. The largest of the buildings towers over the surrounding neighbourhood and is visible from the beach. Its stern architecture is the butt of many popular jokes among the less reverent locals. The complex is lit bright at night with white and red lights.…

spots.name: ExploraScience
spots.desc: Part of the International Centre for Interdisciplinary Science and Education (ICISE) complex, established to further science and research in Vietnam. ExploraScience hosts several exhibitions on Astronomy, Space exploration etc. suitable for children and adults alike.
spots.price: Admission 120,000, purchased on-site only. Tickets are sold 30 minutues prior to opening. Visitors are advised to come…
spots.addr: No.10 Science Avenue, Ghenh Rang Ward

spots.name: Bãi Xép beach and village
spots.desc: With deserted beaches, hilly islands close to shore, and round wooden fishing boats bobbing in the water, the tiny village of Bãi Xép 10 km (6 mi) south of the city centre has become a popular destination for international tourists looking for seaside tranquililty. It's part of the city, but the little hamlet is a world of development away from even sleepy Quy Nhơn's decided lack of buzz and…

spots.name: Beach promenade and city beach
spots.desc: The nicely-maintained beach promenade stretches almost without interruption for 5 km (3 mi) along the southeast coast of Quy Nhơn city. Bordered on both sides by layers of mountains receding into the hazy distance, the natural beauty of the city's waterfront setting has inspired poets for centuries. The contrast to more developed beach resorts such as Nha Trang is stark. Much of the Quy Nhơn…

spots.name: Phương Mai peninsula
spots.desc: The Phương Mai peninsula (see sidebar) is the easiest — and probably only — place in Vietnam to enjoy kilometres of beach in utter solitude. The beach on the northeast side of the peninsula is almost completely empty for over 10 km. Just leave your motorbike anywhere you like on the side of the highway and scramble over the 300-metre wide sand dunes to reach the coast. Take off your shoes and…

spots.name: Beach Promenade Amusement Park
spots.desc: Tiny amusement park squeezed between the trees lining the beach. Semi-permanent rides include a small carousel and wee-sized autos. Squatting vendors offer Vietnamese snack food and painted presents for children. Very low-key atmosphere with beautiful views on the beach and ocean, although the small area can become crowded with local children during high season. The attractions are open to all…

spots.name: Children's World
spots.desc: Bright and cheerful two-storey children's wonderland. Games and fun. Focused on younger children ages 2 to 7.

spots.name: CGV Cinemas
spots.desc: CGV, the only large movie theatre in the city, is in the Big C complex in the far southwest of the city.

spots.name: Carpet football (soccer) and handball
spots.desc: Pick-up and organized games. Teams are informal and welcome newcomers to join in.

spots.name: Happy Billiards
spots.desc: Indoor and outdoor billiards club with nightclub music blasting over massive loudspeakers.

spots.name: Two nicely-maintained tennis hard courts
spots.desc: Often unused. 100,000 dong for one hour, although you are often allowed to enter and play for free.

spots.name: Two volleyball courts (one across the street)
spots.desc: Pick-up games most afternoons and evenings. Low-intermediate skill-level. Visitors very welcome to join in and play.

spots.name: Nguyễn Tất Thành Tennis
spots.desc: Two nicely-maintained hard-surface courts. Courts are unused on most weekday mornings and afternoons. Official price is 100,000 dong for one hour, but you can usually enter and play for free. Evenings from 17:00 to 20:00, a group of 25 male office workers at low-intermediate level play short doubles matches. If you have your own racket, you can join and play with them for free. The courts are…

spots.name: Railway Tennis
spots.desc: Two nicely-maintained red-and-green tennis hard courts in the north centre of the city. Available most mornings and afternoons, including weekends. The fee is 100,000 dong per hour, but you can usually enter and play for free.

spots.name: Sports Complex Tennis
spots.desc: Two nicely-maintained green hard tennis courts for use at the entrance of the sports complex. Available most mornings and afternoons, but usually booked out in the evenings by nearby office workers. 100,000 dong per hour.

spots.name: Victory Club and Châu Thành Billiards
spots.desc: Two large billiards clubs directly across street from each other in a leafy upper-class neighbourhood.

spots.name: An Phú Thịnh Plaza
spots.desc: Multi-storey shopping centre in the east of the city. Low-budget semi-permanent shops offering domestic and imported (mainly from China) clothes, bags, household items. Some electronics.

spots.name: Big C
spots.desc: The Quy Nhơn branch of Thailand's Big C hypermarket lies off Highway 1D close to the Metro bulk store and the bus station in a sparsely-populated area at the foot of the mountains. Offers household products, clothes, and dry foods. The huge building, opened to great fanfare in 2014 for its first-in-the-area green technology, is designed from glass and white aluminium to look like a massive QR…
spots.addr: Kim Cúc Plaza, Quốc Lộ 1D, P. Ghềnh Ráng

spots.name: Coopmart
spots.desc: Opened in 2003, Coopmart is the only supermarket in the city. Offers household products, clothes, and both fresh and packaged food. Compared to Coopmart stores in larger Vietnamese cities, the Quy Nhơn branch has noticeably fewer fresh food products and significantly slower check-out lines. The store serves as the flagship of a local-style shopping centre which covers the entire square block and…
spots.hours: Daily from 08:00–20:00 with no lunch break

spots.name: Metro Cash & Carry
spots.desc: The Quy Nhơn branch of the German-born, Thai-owned self-service bulk wholesaler Metro lies off Highway 1D in a sparsely-populated area at the foot of the mountain in the far south of the city. The yellow-on-blue Metro sign is visible from kilometres away and serves as a reference for drivers in the area.

spots.name: Thể Duc Thể Thao
spots.desc: One of several exercise and fitness store in a one-block area. Sports equipment, athletic apparel, tennis rackets. This block of Lê Hồng Phong is the most convenient — and only — location within a few hundred kilometres to find specialty sports paraphernalia.

spots.name: Văn Hưng
spots.desc: Stylish little store selling imported alcohols, principally whiskies such as Jack Daniels and Johnny Walker.

spots.name: Vĩnh Thụy
spots.desc: One of the only local stores offering a large selection of domestic and imported alcohols.

spots.name: Central Market
spots.desc: Large market in the centre. Consists of a large area partially covered by tarpaulins in the space between Tôn Đức Thắng and Lương Định Của streets, plus vendors — mainly women — spilling out from the covered market area onto both sides of Tôn Đức Thắng street selling fresh fruits and vegetables from blankets. Mangoes, dragonfruit, pineapples, cherimoya, pomelo, coconuts, etc. Unrefrigerated cow…

spots.name: (Covered market) Chợ Đầm
spots.desc: One of the larger and more diversified outdoor markets in Quy Nhơn. In the north centre of city. Fruits and vegetables, freshly cut (and unrefrigerated) beef and chicken. Shellfish. Live chickens and fish. Fireworks products. Incense. Many roving vendors on the surrounding side streets cook bánh xèo on portable charcoal grills. Open from the early morning to evening.

spots.name: Fish market
spots.desc: Outdoor fish market. Vendors — mainly women — sit on low plastic chairs selling freshly-caught fish, shellfish, snails, crabs, lobsters, and oysters from blankets spread on both sides of the street. Usually open in the early morning and late afternoon, but the vendors set their own hours and come and go based on their supply of fish.

spots.name: Indoor/outdoor market
spots.desc: Largest covered food market in the centre of Quy Nhơn. Next to the Minh Tịnh temple and a 10-minute walk west from the Coopmart. The market encompasses a cavernous indoor space housed in a proper building in the area bounded by Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai, Võ Lai, Hàm Nghi and Vũ Bão, as well as an outdoor area on Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai and nearby streets where vendors sell from blankets laid out on the…
spots.addr: centred around Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai and Vũ Bão

spots.name: Bảy Quán
spots.desc: Two-storey restaurant specializing in sizzling steak and eggs (bò neé). Very popular with students and local workers.
spots.price: Combo meal of steak and eggs, salad, soft drink, and bread for 30,000 dong

spots.name: Bê Thui Cầu Mống
spots.desc: Small restaurant offering the famous Quảng Nam specialty of spit-roasted veal. The calf, carefully selected at a young age and at a weight of 30–35 kg (66–77 lb) so as to be not too large and not too small, is roasted whole on a long rod over an open street-side fire of burning charcoal. The blackened skin is then scraped off, and the pink meat is shaved into thin slices and served with salted…

spots.name: Bốn Quang Tuấn
spots.desc: Very good value barbeque/hot-pot restaurant in the centre. Family operation with just six tables. Very popular among students for its low-cost beef and pork barbeque.
spots.price: Pot of clams in spicy sauce 30,000 dong. Hot pot 60,000

spots.name: Hai Thái
spots.desc: Cavernous indoor and outdoor restaurant in the city centre specializing in goat meat. All parts of the goat offered: stomach, intestines, etc. The smell of many goats being grilled simultaneously can be overwhelming if you're not used to it. Private eating rooms available off the main restaurant space.
spots.price: Goat meat on a stick 27,000 dong each. Goat meals 90,000–200,000 dong

spots.name: Hương Việt Cafe
spots.desc: Large upscale cafe and restaurant in the centre, east of Nguyễn Tất Thành and just north of the central market. Beautiful and atmospheric setting where customers sit inside pagoda structures which are connected by wooden bridges and surrounded by topiary and bonsai trees, all accompanied to the sound of classical music from both Europe and Vietnam. Popular with the upper-classes of both local…
spots.price: Coffee 20,000 dong. Tea (several varieties offered) 20,000–25,000. Food prices about 50% higher than same fare at other…

spots.name: Mià Hàng 07
spots.desc: Large seafood restaurant set underneath a semi-covered tin roof in a parking lot on a desolate stretch of road in the southwest of the city. Five-minute walk from the beach. Despite the semi-disreputable appearance (of both the restaurant and the customers), it attracts a loyal local crowd of older intellectuals, who while the day and night away in semi-drunken and fully-rehearsed arguments about…

spots.name: Ốc Biển
spots.desc: Small shellfish-restaurant two blocks north of the beach in the southeast of the city, close to the People's Municipal Building. Eight types of shells daily: grilled oysters, scallops grilled with peanuts and shallots, snails, clams, mussels. Popular with local residents for its prices half those on the nearby beach promenade.

spots.name: Phượng Tèo Bún Chả Cá
spots.desc: Large and very popular low-budget restaurant for fish cake noodle soup.

spots.name: Quán An Cô Bốn Bún Thịt Nướng
spots.desc: Standard Vietnamese local canteen. Pork, chicken, beef stews with rice or noodles. It's neither particularly good nor particularly bad: there are dozens of identical places throughout the city. However, this particular restaurant has become something of a cult-hit among Western tourists to Quy Nhơn after one foreign customer discovered that the owner speaks fairly proficient English thanks to his…
spots.price: 20,000 dong for a plate of rice or noodles with different meat dishes

spots.name: Quán Dê19
spots.desc: Goat-meat in a small corner-restaurant in the city centre. All parts of the goat prepared. Cheaper than larger goat restaurants.

spots.name: Quán Dê35
spots.desc: Goat-meat in a roof-covered, open-air restaurant on the northern riverside shore. Views onto the river, bridge and temple across the water. All parts of the goat prepared.

spots.name: Trần Quang Diệu Shell restaurant
spots.desc: Very good value shellfish dishes. Offers three daily specials of freshly-caught shells: clams, snails, grilled oysters, mussels, scallops, etc. Cooked with spices, garlic, lemongrass, and coconut milk, served on small appetizer-sized plates. Customers sit inside the small space indoors or in a tarpaulin-covered space on the street corner. Very popular at lunchtime among students and local office…
spots.price: Each plate of shells costs 10,000 dong

spots.name: Gia Vỹ
spots.desc: The most famous bánh xèo restaurant in Quy Nhơn has two branches. The largest — and definitely the most touristic — of bánh xèo venues in the city is Gia Vỹ 2, which lies at the northern end of a cluster of four restaurants competing side-by-side on Diên Hồng street. Factory-like in its efficiency and size, circus-like in the bustle of the cooks, waiters, and boys running around trying to corral…

spots.name: Cô Hai bánh xèo
spots.desc: Family-style restaurant offering delicious bánh xèo. Good quality at budget price. A 10-minute walk from the beach on a pleasant, tree-lined street in the southwest of city.

spots.name: Quán An
spots.desc: The largest of several small street-side bánh xèo restaurants in the little night-food area just off the beach promenade on Ngô Văn Sở and surrounding alleys between Nguyễn Huế and Nguyễn Lạc. The bánh xèo is the same at all the restaurants in the small area. Price is highly variable at Quán An; it's one of the very few restaurants in Quy Nhơn which sometimes charge foreigners different prices…

spots.name: Breakfast bánh xèo
spots.desc: Several vendors offer bánh xèo for breakfast in front of their homes on the small, tree-lined street of Trần Quang Diệu between Nguyễn Công Trứ and Tăng Bạt Hổ. They cook daily on most mornings from 07:00 to 10:00, or until they run out of ingredients.

spots.name: Bánh xèo market vendors
spots.desc: Numerous bánh xèo vendors rove the streets around the local market Chợ Đầm in the northern end of the city near the riverside. Very local.

spots.name: Bánh Mì Đất
spots.desc: Local chain of three sandwich shops. Fixed-location stores but no seating. Offers more variety of options than the typical specialized street-side sandwich stall, as well as choice of warming the baguette.

spots.name: Oishi Quán
spots.desc: Hot pot restaurant popular at night with university students. Seating both indoors and at stylish wooden tables on the street.

spots.name: Quyết Thắng
spots.desc: One of many hot-pot restaurants in a small area near the corner of Diên Hồng and Lê Lai. Offers the option of either grilling your food or the traditional style of boiling it in a pot of simmering stock.

spots.name: Buratino
spots.desc: One of the only restaurants in Quy Nhơn — if not the only restaurant — specializing in Western-style food such as pizza and pasta. The restaurant is often recommended by the bigger hotels to Western tourists looking for comfort food similar to home. But it's a small restaurant and Quy Nhơn is not an international city, so the food is suited to local tastes and ends up being more Vietnamese-style…
spots.price: Dishes from 50,000–100,000 dong, combo meals 200,000–270,000 dong

spots.name: KFC
spots.desc: The only Western fast-food chain restaurant in the city, in the southeast corner of the Coopmart shopping centre.

spots.name: NamSushi
spots.desc: Large and elaborate sushi restaurant. Two storeys: the lower floor seating is at normal tables, while the upper floor has views towards the sea and seating on pillows and a no-shoes-allowed shiny hardwood floor. The quality of the food might not be at the standards of sushi in Tokyo (or Beijing, Moscow or Los Angeles), but it's the best and most modern sushi in the not-so-international-yet Quy…
spots.price: Tuna maki 40,000 dong, sushi 30,000–80,000 for two pieces, temaki salmon hand roll 45,000. Basic combo sushi sets…

spots.name: Pizza H-P
spots.desc: Small pizza restaurant in the city centre with the English-language motto "Be Different". Offers hot pot and Western pizzas done Vietnamese style.

spots.name: Pop Gelato
spots.desc: Modern gelatto shop in west of city. Popular with young people.

spots.name: An Bình
spots.desc: Mid-sized vegetarian just north of the temple. Slightly more upscale setting than most vegetarian restaurants in the city, with tablecloths and flowers on each table. Open hours officially 07:00–21:00, although often closes for long breaks. One of several vegetarian restaurants near the Long Khánh Buddhist temple.
spots.price: Vegetarian bánh xèo 10,000 dong. Plate of daily vegetable dishes with rice 18,000 dong

spots.name: Hiển Nam
spots.desc: Medium-large vegetarian attached to the Hiển Nam temple just west of Nguyễn Tất Thành street. A four-minute walk from Coopmart. Picturesque views of the temple through the open back gate of the restaurant.
spots.price: Daily lunch of rice with several vegetable dishes plus soup: 15,000

spots.name: Kim Ngọc Bánh Mì
spots.desc: A permanent street stall one block south of Minh Tịnh temple selling vegetarian baguette sandwiches (bánh mì).

spots.name: Nhà hàng
spots.desc: Very large vegetarian restaurant on the south side of Long Khánh Buddhist temple. Dependably open long hours from morning until night, including holidays. Slightly more expensive than the many smaller, family-run vegetarian restaurants in the area.

spots.name: Pháp Duyên
spots.desc: Mid-sized vegetarian one block southeast of the Minh Tịnh temple. A five-minute walk from either the central plaza on the beach or from the Coopmart.

spots.name: Sáu Thu
spots.desc: Mid-size vegetarian restaurant next to the Quy Nhơn Evangelical Church in the eastern end of the central city. Both the setting and the food are a slight step above similar vegetarian venues.
spots.price: One plate of assorted vegetable dishes plus rice 30,000 dong

spots.name: Thanh Minh
spots.desc: Small family-run vegetarian restaurant on the north side of Long Khánh Buddhist temple. Generally offers several vegetable-based dishes, as opposed to the meat-substitute dishes found at typical Vietnamese vegetarian restaurants.
spots.price: Mixed vegetable dishes, rice and soup: 20,000 dong

spots.name: Thanh Tấm
spots.desc: Mid-sized vegetarian restaurant one block south of the Minh Tịnh temple.
spots.price: Daily lunch of mixed vegetables including rice and soup for 15,000 dong

spots.name: Thanh Vân
spots.desc: Very tiny vegetarian restaurant in a family-home in a small alley off the main street. One of several vegetarian restaurants near the Long Khánh Buddhist temple.

spots.name: Tịnh Tâm
spots.desc: Small family-run vegetarian just north of the Long Khánh temple. One of several vegetarian restaurants near the temple. Extremely kind family owners often invites foreigners to explore their home and culture.

spots.name: Bánh Kem Ngọc Nga
spots.desc: The largest, most elaborate — and commensurately most expensive — bakery in Quy Nhơn. Intricately designed and decorated cakes, for example shaped as animals (frogs, dogs, bunnies, dragons) and human figures (Buddha, princesses). Cake flavors include green tea (matcha), tiramisu, and standard cream cakes. Also offers vegan (pure-veg) baked products. The bakery spans three adjacent stores, with…
spots.price: Mid-size cakes 60,000–200,000 dong, larger and more elaborate cakes 200,000–400,000. Cookies and chocolates 5,000–15,000

spots.name: Đúc Tỏ Baguette Bakers
spots.desc: Long-standing family operation that bakes the baguettes used for bánh mì sandwiches. Reputed among locals to be the highest quality baguettes in the city.
spots.price: 1,300 dong for one hot baguette fresh out of the oven, 15,000 for 12

spots.name: Phương Ngá Bakery
spots.desc: Small bakery offering cakes and chocolate pieces. Offers all the standard cakes and decorations, with a specialty in tiramisu cakes and fruit-jelly cakes (including passion-fruit cake). Unusually for Quy Nhơn, sells pieces of cakes in single servings, rather than entire cakes.
spots.price: Whole cakes 50,000–150,000 dong. Single-serving piece of cake 10,000–20,000. Chocolate letters (for spelling out words…

spots.name: Tamba Bakery
spots.desc: Spacious and clean bakery in the southwest of city with the English motto "Good Food — Good Life." Cakes, cupcakes, cream buns, pork floss buns. Prices around 20–40% less than most Quy Nhơn bakeries.

spots.name: Tinh Hoa Bakery
spots.desc: Corner bakery very popular among locals for birthdays, holidays, and family meals.
spots.price: Cakes 50,000–200,000 dong. Cupcakes 15,000. Chocolate hearts 5,000. Squares of coconut and sticky rice in powdered…

spots.name: Bookafe
spots.desc: Very large higher-end cafe with both outdoor and indoor seating. Three minutes by foot southwest from the Coopmart. Extensive lighting in the evening makes it a popular spot for couples at night. Gelatto ice cream available. Somewhat confusingly, the cafe's name is spelled "Bookafe" on internet sites and Facebook, but the logo is designed as "Bookkafe", where the middle "k" is stylized to be both…

spots.name: Búp Cafe
spots.desc: Small and cute cafe in the city centre a 10-minute walk northwest from the beach or seven minutes west from Coopmart. Beloved by teenage girls for its cute drinks, caramel popcorn, and Western pop music. The friendy owner Búp, one of the very few cafe owners in the city completely fluent in English, converted his parents' small clothing store into the eponymous cafe in the summer of 2015 after…
spots.price: Milk tea 17,000 dong plus 3,000 for toppings

spots.name: Đất Việt Cafe
spots.desc: Charming cafe built underneath — and hidden amongst — towering trees on a quiet lane a 7-minute walk west from the beach in the southwest of the city.

spots.name: Du Mục Cafe
spots.desc: Pleasant indoor cafe decorated with many tropical plants on the walls and bamboo-mat hanging from the ceilings. It's in the city centre on an idyllic, narrow street packed with bonsai trees, flags and children playing.

spots.name: G.Life Cafe
spots.desc: Hipster-esque cafe in the northern end of the city. White-brick wall interior. Offers ice coffee blended with tiramisu, cookies or banana.
spots.price: Coffee 10,000 dong, latte 21,000, cappuccino 21,000. Blended ice coffee 25,000. Smoothies 25,000. Cookies and cream…

spots.name: Helen Cafe
spots.desc: Cute little cafe near Chùa Trúc Lâm temple. Popular among local teenage girls for its milk tea, bubble tea, iced coffee, and cookies drinks. Seating on pillows on the floor. Walls decorated with bright pink drawings, hipster black-and-white photos, and enormous paintings of Japan and Europe.
spots.price: Milk tea 20,000 dong plus 3,000 for each topping

spots.name: Hello Kitty Cafe
spots.desc: All the Hello Kitty drinks, cakes and sweets you could want in a cafe with all the Hello Kitty decorations you could squeeze into a small space. Ignore the trademark violations (shhhh...) and enjoy.

spots.name: Inn Cafe
spots.desc: Peaceful indoor cafe with picturesque European-style window boxes and white window frames. A two-minute walk south of the central market on Tôn Đức Thắng street.

spots.name: Jolly
spots.desc: Cafe with a young and modern style in the east of the city. With fishbowl windows facing on the street corner giving lots of natural light, white brick walls, gelato bar, and an extensive menu of cookie drinks, frappuccinos, smoothies, and tea with jam, Jolly has attracted a steady crowd of young people since its 2015 opening. Adorning the walls are chalk-scribbled translations of Vietnamese…
spots.price: Coffee and smoothie drink mixes 20,000–30,000 dong

spots.name: Like Cafe
spots.desc: City centre cafe near the central food market. The modern decor and creative drinks makes it popular with Quy Nhơn's (very small) young and fashionable crowd. Large outdoor seating area, plus indoor tables. One of the nicer public bathroom in Quy Nhơn (damning with faint praise, but modern clean toilets aren't one of Quy Nhơn's specialties).
spots.price: Coffee 20,000-25,000 dong, cacao with yogurt cubes 40,000, smoothies 35,000-45,000

spots.name: Marina Cafe
spots.desc: Mid-market, modern-style cafe in the southwest corner of the An Phú Thịnh Plaza building.

spots.name: Osaka Cafe
spots.desc: Multi-storey cafe in the centre. A two-minute walk east from the airport shuttle bus drop-off. Typical large mid-budget Vietnamese style cafe/restaurant. Nothing to do with Japan other than the name and a painting of Mt. Fuji. Large indoor water-pond display with dozens of small porcelain Buddhas playing under plastic cherry blossoms. Karaoke on upper floors. Big open windows on street. Old but…

spots.name: p.u.q. Cafe
spots.desc: Hip little cafe in the centre. The decor is a mix between urban industrial and Asian kitsch. Stylish smoothies served in an edible glass made of sweet jelly.

spots.name: Queen Cafe
spots.desc: Pleasant two-storey treehouse-cafe a 10-minute walk northwest from the beach.

spots.name: Reform Cafe
spots.desc: Industrial-style hipster-esque coffee shop. Complete with intricate latte art and baristas wielding tough attitudes, Reform cafe could (almost) be at home in London, Paris or Brooklyn. Small indoor and outdoor space. Smokey. Offers more varieties of coffee drinks than most cafes in Quy Nhơn.
spots.price: Espresso 15,000 dong, Irish cafe 20,000, latte 25,000, mocha 28,000, cappuccino 25,000

spots.name: Sam Cafe
spots.desc: Very large outdoor cafe set rather unusually amidst dozens of bonsai trees which are for sale. At the entrance waits a human-sized statue of a fisher goddess to greet you.

spots.name: Tien Loi Coffee
spots.desc: Tiny and sweet cafe a block north of the Long Khánh temple in the northeast of the city centre. Small outdoor seating. Milk tea and coffee served in artsy jars tied off with burlap rope designs. Specialty drink of red and green Thai sweet tea. The upstairs has a no-shoes pillow-seating area surrounded by massive posters illustrating Vietnamese fantasy stories.

spots.name: Violet Cafe
spots.desc: Very pleasant, modern cafe. Wood tables and chairs. Has a glass-enclosed non-smoking room with pillow-seating on a sparkling-clean hardwood floor. Drinks only, no food.

spots.name: Style Pub & Bar
spots.desc: The biggest nightclub in Quy Nhơn. The only one, as well. Lots of blue and green neon lights. Lots of smoke, both from cigarettes and from smoke machines. Mainly Vietnamese music, loud and with the bass cranked up, but some Western pop mixed in.

spots.name: Eatu Café
spots.desc: Fair trade coffee cooperative and manufacturer, funded by the European Union. Open for visits.
spots.addr: 22 KT Street, Ko Tam village, Eatu commune

spots.name: Lady Jiangshan
spots.desc: Breathtaking views from the hill top and halfway to the top. Well worth a visit on the way to Lak Lake.

spots.name: Phượng shop
spots.desc: Wood sculptures and bamboo souvenirs, cocoa powder, coffee - ground and in beans, assorted nuts and local spices. Tour to coffee roasting factory can be arranged.

spots.name: Vincom Plaza
spots.desc: Big shopping center with clothing stores, movie theater, fast food, supermarket and Baskin Robbins ice cream cafe. No local souvenirs there.

spots.name: CoopMart
spots.desc: Supermarket and shopping center, check second floor if you are looking for non-food items. KFC restaurant is located on the first floor.

spots.name: Mehyco cafe
spots.desc: Another cafe with a nice garden, belonging to a coffee manufacturing company.

spots.name: Cultural museum of Vietnam ethnic minority groups
spots.local: Bảo tàng Văn hóa các Dân tộc Việt Nam
spots.desc: Kind of a smaller version of the ethnographic museum of Hanoi.

spots.name: Đài phun nước TP. Thái Nguyên
spots.desc: Multi-colored fountain right in front of the cultural museum that is a gathering point in the evening.

spots.name: Quảng trường Võ Nguyên Giáp
spots.desc: a nationalist type monument with hourglass-like obelisk and town square.

spots.name: Nui Coc Lake
spots.desc: a lake featuring an amusement park on a hill, water park, boat rides, extreme sport activities, sunsets behind tea plantations, and musical water performances. Kind of like a Vietnamese ecotourism area on steroids with concrete Buddhas and dragons everywhere.
spots.addr: Tan Thai Commune Dai Tu District

spots.name: Mekong Boat Tour
spots.desc: The thing to do in Vinh Long. A typical trip includes the floating market at Cai Be and An Binh Islands lasting about 4 hr.

spots.name: Visit An Binh
spots.desc: If you are on budget or you already have done enough boat tours, you can go to An Binh on the ferry (1000 dong, one-way) and either walk on the main islands (small bridges connect nearly all the islands), rent bicycle/moto or pay a mototaxi (40-60,000 dong per hour). Bonsai garden is about 20 min from the ferry pier by motorbike. Near the pier there is a Chinese temple and a school, a bit further…

spots.name: Watpo Yoga Centre
spots.desc: Clean and modern yoga centre and wellness spa.

spots.name: Tan Phát
spots.desc: Small store selling imported Hennessy and Belvedere.

spots.name: Cửa hàng Đặc sản hải sản tươi khô
spots.desc: Traditional local specialties, fresh/dry seafood.

spots.name: Bánh Xèo Tôm Nhảy Gia Vỹ
Bánh Xèo Tôm Nhảy Gia Vy 2. 14 Diên Hồng
Jollibee
spots.desc: The Philippine fast-food chain.

spots.name: Minh Hoa
spots.desc: Standard mid-size vegetarian restaurant.
spots.price: Plate of vegetable dishes with rice plus soup 15,000 dong

spots.name: Hoàng Yến Bakery
spots.desc: Small bakery offering big cakes.

spots.name: Cua Tu Waterfall
spots.desc: somewhat dirty forest waterfall

spots.name: Phuong Hoang Cave
spots.desc: Riverine cave system and karst formations.

spots.name: Thai Hai Reserve Area of Ecological Houses-on-stilts Ethnic Village
spots.local: Khu bảo tồn Làng nhà sàn Dân tộc Sinh thái Thái Hải
spots.desc: Stilt village ethnic tour.
spots.addr: Khu du lịch Thái Hải, Thịnh Đức

spots.name: Tan Cuong Tea Cultural Center
spots.local: Không gian văn hóa trà Thái Nguyên
spots.desc: Tea farm tours.
spots.addr: Tân Cương, Thành phố Thái Nguyên

spots.name: Mine Action Visitor Center
spots.desc: Excellent museum on the on-going effects of UXO (unexploded ordnance) in the DMZ area.

spots.name: Museum of Quan Tri province
spots.desc: Museum providing detailed information about the region, its history (including the Vietnam War), culture, local life and industries.

spots.name: Tran Hung Dao St Market
spots.desc: One of the largest markets of the country. People can easily find affordable goods and souvenirs here, most of which are from China and Thailand. Travellers never want to miss this place when they visit Dong Ha.

spots.name: Tam's Cafe
spots.desc: Excellent coffee and selection of drinks, some good Western food and basic Vietnamese dishes. Very helpful owner can arrange tours and help with anything you may need. Good place to meet other travellers in town.

spots.name: General museum of Quảng Ngãi Province
spots.desc: Contains cultural artifacts of Sa Huynh & Champa civilizations, and other ethnic minorities of Quẚng Ngãi Province.

spots.name: Ly Son Island
spots.desc: Ly Son Island is 26 km (14 nautical miles) from Sa Ky Port. The island is about 10 km² and known as the Garlic Capital of Central Vietnam. There are traces of the ancient Sa Huynh and Champa cultures on the island. The local people live by farming and fishing. There are several beautiful spots on the island such as Cave Pagoda, An Hai Village temple, Hoang Sa Museum, and two volcanic mouths Gieng…

spots.name: My Khe Beach
spots.desc: My Khe Beach is one of the best beaches in Quẚng Ngãi. It is about 8 km long with fine, white, and smooth powdery sands. Behind the beach is a green poplar forest creating a green space of hundreds hectares running along the internal tourist area. My Khe Tourist Resort is in this area. There are several food stalls erected along the beach, catering mostly to locals. This beach has yet to…

spots.name: Mỹ Lai Massacre Memorial Museum
spots.desc: A memorial to 504 victims killed in 1969 by US forces in the My Lai incident. The site is a solemn place and also the main reason foreign visitors choose to stop by this province. To get to the museum is easy; you just need to take the local bus (line: SAKI) from Quang Ngai downtown, in front of the Hotel Khách Sạn Hùng Vương (address: 45 Hùng Vương, tp. Quảng Ngãi, Quảng Ngãi, Vietnam). This…

spots.name: Sa Huynh Beach
spots.desc: Sa Huynh is a beautiful beach with clear water and golden sand. Sa Huynh is also called Sa Hoang, means "gold sand" as the color of the sand is not white like some other places but is a glittered yellow sand. A popular stopover location for travelers to spend a few days on the beach, bordered by coconut groves and rice paddies, before continuing their journey.

spots.name: The Long Wall of Quẚng Ngãi
spots.desc: A version of the Hadrian's Wall. Discovered in 2005, the Long Wall of Quẚng Ngãi is a majestic architectural construction that remains in its original state. Built over 500 years mainly with stones and earth, with an average high of 2 m, the wall spans over 113 km with several forts, roads, and military depots. The Wall was constructed in the early days by the Viet settlers when this region was…

spots.name: Thien An Mountain
spots.desc: Squared in shape likes a seal hence the name Thien An (Heaven's Seal). This small mountain is revered by the locals as a spiritual place. A three-century-old pagoda sits near the top and at the summit is the tomb of the region's famous anti-colonial hero Huynh Thuc Khang.

spots.name: Thien But Mountain
spots.desc: Travelers to Quẚng Ngãi often inquired about Thien But Mountain along with its higher cousin Thien An Mountain. However, Thien But Mountain is more renowned in poetry rather than in reality. A small hill that rises 60 m high above the coastal plains. On a clouds covered day, Thien But Mountain looks like a calligraphy brush with its tip dipped into the clouds hence the name Thien But (Heaven's…

spots.name: Bike ride Co Luy Commune
spots.desc: Visitors often ask where Co Luy Commune is. This area was once renowned in poetry and claimed to be second only to Hue for its bucolic, rustic rural charms. The area is slowly giving way to development. However, one can still find its coconut groves, its swaying pine trees, and meandering streams. Folks come here just to see whether it is as described in the poetry they once heard in schools.…

spots.name: Coop Mart Quẚng Ngãi
spots.desc: A department store with typical household items, clothing, grocery, and gifts. Air-conditioned so a good way to escape the heat and shop.

spots.name: Quẚng Ngãi Market
spots.desc: The main market of Quẚng Ngãi. Has everything from household goods to grocery. A typical market as can be found in many towns. There are also eating stalls in the market.

spots.name: Catholic Seminary
spots.desc: Houses a small minority museum, but the colonial-style building itself is well worth a visit.

spots.name: Montagnard Church
spots.desc: Built in 1913 and restored in the 1990s. It is remarkable for its blending of local artistic tradition and Christian symbols: Bahnar villages, elephants, a scale model of a rong.

spots.name: Kon Tum Tourist
spots.desc: If you are on a tight itinerary, it might be good to fix things beforehand, since they are often crowded with tour groups. Though some of the Bahnar villages actually form a part of Kontum's eastern and western edge, the ones farther away are more interesting. Highlights would be the different kinds of rong, the cemeteries of the Jarai, and joining a rice-wine party with the locals.

spots.name: Dakbla Restaurant
spots.desc: Separate from the hotel of the same name, Dakbla is nicely themed with decorations from the surrounding minority peoples. Wide variety of food including local and Western staples, excellent wild boar. Popular with tourists. English spoken.

spots.name: Cafe Eva
spots.desc: Home to a local artist and a lot of his oeuvre is on display in the garden and the three-storey house resembling a stilt house. The place is a favourite among Vietnamese locals. The owner, Mr. An can also share in-depth knowledge of the Montagnards' culture and arrange day tours of Bahnar villages or explorations of indigenous culture, with local homestays.

spots.name: Sunrise Café
spots.desc: Quiet two-storey café with good coffee and honest and nice staff.

spots.name: Bắc Hà Sunday Market
spots.desc: Bắc Hà Sunday market can be visited from Sa Pa, but is nearer to Lào Cai and best visited just after you have arrived in Lào Cai from Hanoi or when you have returned to Lào Cai to take the train back to Hanoi.

spots.name: Church of Our Lady of the Rosary
spots.local: Nhà Thờ Đức Mẹ Mân Côi; Église Notre-Dame du Rosaire
spots.desc: A Roman Catholic church established by the French and constructed between 1926 and 1935. Mass is held on weekdays at 19:00 and on Sunday at 09:00, and the adoration of the sacrament is held at 18:30.

spots.name: Hàm Rồng Resort
spots.desc: A hillside attraction with great views and various gardens such as an orchid garden and a European garden, ethnic minority dance performances, and restaurants.

spots.name: Sa Pa Culture Museum
spots.desc: If you have time, the museum is worth visiting to learn about the history of Sa Pa, and the costumes and traditions of the ethnic minorities of the region.

spots.name: Sa Pa Square
spots.desc: The square is hard to miss. It is a centre of local activity. Often in the evenings, you may see the locals gather for shopping and selling, or playing a game of foot-badminton in groups. You may see dances in the square.

spots.name: Cát Cát village
spots.desc: This walk provides a good chance to observe Vietnamese farming and farm animals, and there are excellent views. It's a few kilometers' walk from Sa Pa. You're not likely to get lost: just walk down the road out of Sa Pa, which should be marked on maps. After a while, you'll find a path which descends the hill to your left. This path runs through the village before climbing another hill back to…
spots.price: Admission: 70,000 dong, 30,000 dong for children under 10 year-old

spots.name: Hoàng Liên National Park, Love Waterfall and Silver Waterfall
spots.desc: Love Waterfall (Thác Tình Yêu), which lies within Hoàng Liên National Park (Vườn quốc gia Hoàng Liên; declared an ASEAN Heritage Park). It takes 30 minutes to walk from the entrance of the park to the waterfall. The path is paved with flat but slightly uneven stones and has many steps going up and down. there are many shaded areas for rest along the way. Silver Waterfall (Thác Bạc), regarded by…
spots.price: Hoàng Liên National Park: 70,000 dong; Silver Waterfall: 20,000 dong

spots.name: Massage
spots.desc: Numerous shops along Cầu Mây Street, the town's main street, provide foot and body massages. Many hotels also offer in-room massages.

spots.name: Phan Si Păng
spots.desc: At 3,143 m (10,312 ft), Phan Si Păng or Fansipan is the highest mountain in Indochina (Cambodia, Laos and Vietnam), and lies within the Hoàng Liên National Park (Vườn quốc gia Hoàng Liên). Hikes to the summit lasting from 1-3 days can be arranged from tour companies in Sa Pa. Most of them recommend taking the 2- or 3-day options; few guides will take tourists on the round trip in a single day. A…

spots.name: Fansipan Legend
spots.desc: The cable car up Fansipan offering a rather less strenuous route up the tallest mountain in Indochina. The views are often obscured by the fog.
spots.price: 750,000 dong, 550,000 dong for children between 1 and 1.4 m; 100,000 dong for the funicular from Sapa Town (Hotel…

spots.name: Sa Pa Lake
spots.desc: The lake is within walking distance of the city center. At the lake you can rent a pedal boat for 40,000 dong for 30 minutes, or 80,000 dong for an hour. Pedal boats are available only on weekends and when the weather is good.

spots.name: Simacai Market
spots.desc: Of all Sa Pa markets, Simacai Market may well best demonstrate traditional customs and habits which have not been affected by tourist commercialization.

spots.name: The Hill Station Signature
spots.desc: Refined local (mostly Hmong) food in small dishes - the speciality, if they have found fresh fish that day, is their raw trout. Perched on the edge of the valley, some tables have views right across it. A few decent options for vegetarians.

spots.name: The Hill Station Deli
spots.desc: Fine wine, cheese and cold cuts of meat along with a few western style hot and cold dishes. Home-made hams and pâté. Punto Italia coffee.

spots.name: Little View Restaurant
spots.desc: A popular, low-priced restaurant. Serves outstanding local and decent Western dishes to a mixed local and foreign clientele. Features some unique dishes in addition to the fixtures available at any other Sa Pa restaurant. Try the hot pot with salmon.

spots.name: Marketplace food stalls
spots.desc: Food stalls selling good noodle soup for 10,000 dong, fried rice for 15,000 dong and the other usual Vietnamese fare for around 30,000 dong. It's a great experience to dine with the locals.

spots.name: Rose Garden Sa Pa
spots.desc: A mid-range restaurant. They have freshly baked baguettes and hamburgers from their own bakery. The desserts, ice cream, cakes, and cookies, are sweet delicacies at an affordable price.

spots.name: Hoa Tam Vegetarian Restaurant
spots.desc: One of the rare vegetarian restaurants in town, hidden in a small street close to the church, down the stairs.

spots.name: Cong Caphe
spots.desc: Coffee place that also serves some food. Lots of drinks available: coffee, tea, coconut milk (the one with coffee being their signature drink), yoghurt & beer. Food includes pizza, cocooned sweet potato & bamboo-cooked rice. Nice chilling atmosphere (thanks to the music & quite big space available). Staff speak decent English. While drinks & food are modern, entering the place you feel like…

spots.name: Bich Dong Pagoda
spots.desc: Three temples carved into a limestone mountain, dating from the 15th-century reign of Le Thai To. The lower temple has a stone next to it that resonates when tapped, plus a Buddha footprint. The middle temple has an 18th-century bell, a cave and resonating pillars. The top temple has a view of the surrounding countryside, which is good for sunsets.
spots.price: Free. Parking 20,000 dong, or free on the square in front of the entrance bridge if you buy a drink for 25,000 dong, or…

spots.name: Hidden Valley (Secret Cave)
spots.desc: Only very few tourists wander into this secluded valley. There is a shop selling some drinks and ice cream, but which might be closed. There is a boat advertising a tour into a 350m deep cave, a wide peaceful field with some goats and then there is the 15min walking tour through a cave. The guide babbles about in Vietnamese only, shows various fossil shells and funny shaped wall markings…
spots.price: Cave tour 30,000 dong, boat tour 50,000 dong

spots.name: Mua Cave
spots.desc: The cave here is an afterthought; the main draws are the two hilltop viewpoints. 500 steps will lead you to the first peak, an unimpressive temple with incredibly stunning views over Tam Coc and Ninh Binh’s countryside, including a large lotus flower field at the bottom (should bloom in June/July). On the second slightly higher peak, there is a long dragon statue which you can climb…
spots.price: 100,000 dong entrance fee + 10,000 dong bicycle/motorbike parking fee

spots.name: Thung Nham Bird Park
spots.desc: Entrance ticket includes two boat rides, one in a cave with sleeping bats and one to the conservation bird park. Some very beautiful flower gardens, tree areas and bamboo bridges. You are allowed to bring your own bicycle inside and cycle around. Useful too as its about 1.3km from ticket office to park entrance with a steep hill to get over.
spots.addr: Hai Nham, Ninh Hai, Tam Coc

spots.name: Dundj Valley
spots.desc: A quieter limestone valley located beyond the main tourist routes of Tam Coc, with rice fields, small waterways, and surrounding karst formations. The area is characterized by a rural landscape where visitors may encounter farming activities, grazing animals, and narrow paths connecting small plots of land. In some parts of the valley, waterways extend into natural cave sections, including a…

spots.name: Tam Coc Museum
spots.desc: A small museum presenting aspects of traditional Vietnamese rural life. Exhibits include rice cultivation, grain processing, and traditional tools used in farming communities.

spots.name: Khe Coc Island
spots.desc: The former filming location of the village from Kong: Skull Island, repurposed in 2024 as an outdoor cultural museum. There isn't much there yet.
spots.price: 20,000 dong, 300,000 dong combo ticket with Trang An

spots.name: Bear Sanctuary Ninh Binh
spots.desc: It was built by the animal welfare organisation Four Paws opened for visitors in 2019. It covers 5.5 ha, and plans to expand to 10 ha and open an education centre. Different from other sanctuaries, visitors will not be able to enter the whole sanctuary. A path leads the visitors above some enclosures to allow them to observe the bears from a distance.
spots.addr: Cuc Phuong - Bai Dinh Rd, Ky Phu commune, Nho Quan district

spots.name: Trang An
spots.local: Tràng An, Trang An Ecotourism Complex
spots.desc: The most extensive waterway tour in Ninh Binh. Many tourists prefer this trip to Tam Coc as there are many more caves to pass through and not as many hawkers. After buying a ticket, find your way to the boarding area, and decide on your route. (Do not agonize over your decision, as each route includes plenty of temples, caves, and landscapes.) Each is about 3 hours, so make sure to carry sun…
spots.price: 250,000 dong. Parking fee of 15,000 dong for motorbikes or free for bicycles

spots.name: Trung Tuyet Restaurant
spots.desc: A few tables on the street and one of the few restaurants in the city that caters to Westerners. The menu offers 3 or 4 sizes of portions at different prices, however even the small sized portions are larger than in other towns. Coffee 20,000 dong, Fruit salad 30,000 dong. Yogurt 8,000 dong. Chicken with noodles 50,000 dong.

spots.name: Pho bò 24
spots.desc: A small restaurant for locals with the food cooked in front of you. A few tables on the street and few inside. Soups and noodle for 25,000 dong and 30,000 dong. Have an English menu.

spots.name: Aroma Indian Restaurant
spots.desc: Indian restaurant which is one of the few in town to have air-con. Excellent Indian food and snappy service. Enormous nan breads! Very reasonable prices given the quality.

spots.name: Chookie's Beer Garden
spots.desc: Great place to relax and have a drink and something to eat away from the main street. Good burgers, salads and Smoothies. Plenty of vegan options too. Has a nice veggie garden and play area. The have another outlet called Chookie Coop, near Mua Cave.

spots.name: Thang Long Restaurant
spots.desc: Large restaurant serving local mountain goat dishes, com chay (crispy rice) and hill chicken. Several big dining halls take tour groups, and there is a car park. Set menus can be arranged in advance.
spots.addr: Chi Phong hamlet, Tay Hoa Lu

spots.name: Dive! Dive! Dive!
spots.desc: Daily dive and snorkelling trips from a 15-m custom-built dive boat or 5-m speedboat. Opened in 2010 and affiliated with SSI, owned by an American. Having completed more than 1,000 dives on the islands, there is simply nobody who knows the diving better. They are the only full-time resident expats and the only fully Western-owned and operated business on the island. Turtle trips in season.…

spots.name: Rainbow Divers
spots.desc: PADI dive centre operating out of the Six Senses Resort on Dat Doc Beach. They offer daily dive trips.

spots.name: Turtle Sanctuary
spots.desc: The turtle tour can be booked at the national park office. You may see a turtle laying eggs. Turtle season is only from Jun-early September. Turtles are likely only nesting in Jul-Aug with a few hatchlings still coming out in September. The park will happily sell you tickets out of season and promise turtles. The trip is not cheap. Be aware and do not fall for this. Do not book a turtle tour…

spots.name: Con Dao Dive Center
spots.desc: Con Dao Dive Center is a PADI Dive Center located on Con Dao Island, Vietnam. The center provides scuba diving, snorkeling, freediving, and PADI certification courses, operating with certified PADI instructors and regularly maintained equipment in accordance with PADI standards and local marine park regulations. The center also supports marine conservation initiatives, including sea turtle…

spots.name: Noodle Shop
spots.desc: For lunchtime, you can also find some local restaurants that serve good noodle soups for 15,000 dong. This is one of them.

spots.name: Phuong Han
spots.desc: Popular with the tourist crowd. Atmosphere needs some work, but the food is good and it is reasonably priced. Very popular for lunch.

spots.name: Tri Ky
spots.desc: Offers tasty, fresh seafood at reasonable prices, and has an English menu available, although offerings are relatively sparse.

spots.name: Bar200
spots.desc: Near the market, and associated with Senses diving, serves decent Western food, cocktails and good breakfasts.

spots.name: Vinh Trang Pagoda
spots.desc: Vinh Trang Pagoda is in a large garden in My Phong Commune. The architecture of the pagoda is a harmonious combination of Asian and European types of architecture, creating the splendid, but simple features of this Buddhist pagoda. Vinh Trang Pagoda is the greatest pagoda of Tien Giang Province.

spots.name: Cao Dai Temple
spots.desc: Most tourists arrive for the noon mass. There is a balcony that runs along the walls halfway up. This is where you can watch the service. It is a very nice view. There is an orchestra of approximately 10 musicians whose music is traditionally Vietnamese. A choir of approximately 20 lead the congregation in the prayers. The musical mix of the hymns is very unusual with a blend of Western and…

spots.name: Dau Tieng Reservoir
spots.desc: It was constructed in 1981 to provide water in Tay Ninh province as well as neighboring provinces. The lake covers an area of 27,000 hectares, and it contains up to 1.5 billion m³ of water. The reservoir is set in a beautiful landscape of surrounding of mountains with many islets.

spots.name: Lo Go Xa Mat National Park
spots.desc: A short ride from Tay Ninh lays the remnant of a primeval forest that used to cover much of land in Tay Ninh province. Covered 18,675 ha and comprised of lowland forests and wetlands, Lo Go Xa Mat National Park was established in 2002 as a nature reserve. The park boasts a rich biodiversity of flora and fauna, some of which are endangered species. The only protected natural reserve in Tay Ninh…

spots.name: Ba Den Mountain
spots.desc: This mountain is considered the roof of southern Vietnam and often called van son or cloud mountain because it is always covered by clouds. The mountain is made up of three smaller mountains called Heo (pig), Phung (phoenix), and Ba Den (black lady). There is a trip cable car from the bottom of the mountain to the top. Or you can walk the trail. The views of the countryside are breathtaking.…

spots.name: Feed the Monkeys
spots.desc: There are monkeys living in trees on the temple grounds. Feeding the monkeys is a favorite activity for the locals and visitors alike. One can see them dashing about near the seating arenas on the two sides of the big square in front of the temple. Peanuts, fruits, and whatever edible are thrown to the monkeys.

spots.name: Walk the Rubber Plantation
spots.desc: There are large tracts of rubber plantations all over Tay Ninh, however, you can visit one right inside the Holy See, saving you the need to go anywhere far. Tracts of rubber fields are planted throughout the Holy See complex. You can take a stroll in any of these fields to experience the production of a rubber plantation in Tay Ninh.

spots.name: Conquer Ba Den Peak
spots.desc: For the adventurous souls who wish to reach the very summit of Ba Den Mountain, the 360-degree vista of the surrounding countryside is the ultimate reward. Perching 986 m above sea level, the summit offers a good day's hike. Take a taxi or motorbike taxi halfway up the mountain near the temples entrances. From there, it is a good 2 hr hike to the top. At the summit, some climbing skills are…

spots.name: Chilli Salts
spots.desc: Tay Ninh is famous for its unique chilli salts. Crushed to a powder, chilli peppers are mixed with salt and seasonings to make chilli salts. Spicy and salty, a good dipping for fruits and snacks or sprinkled on foods. Sold practically everywhere in Tay Ninh, especially on roadsides coming in/out of town.

spots.name: Long Hoa Market
spots.desc: Long Hoa Market sells food, clothing and everything else you would expect to find in a marketplace.

spots.name: Cánh Ký Noodle House
spots.desc: Family-owned for more than 20 years. This noodle house is well-known to locals. Famous for their won ton noodle soups.

spots.name: Phở Mai
spots.desc: A decent place to find a good bowl of phở (beef noodle soup). Clean place. Fast service.

spots.name: Tùng Ký Noodle
spots.desc: Small, but busy noodle house serving delicious won ton noodles.

spots.name: Cafe Bang Lang
spots.desc: Large open space and plenty of seating. This place can be crowded with bureaucrats and office workers in the early morning due to its proximity to all the government and business buildings.

spots.name: Cafe Thao Wind
spots.desc: This place offers plenty of tropical greens and misty vapours to cool the soul. Overhead swaying baskets of tropical plants form a natural canopy and trickling water fountains cool the air. A nice place to chill and pass the time.

spots.name: Smiling Buddha
spots.desc: A happy Buddha statue that is almost 50 feet tall.
spots.addr: Nam Ban, Lam Ha, Lam Dong

spots.name: Me Linh Coffee Garden
spots.desc: Surrounded by coffee plantation
spots.addr: To 20 thon 4, Ta Nung, Tp. Da Lạt, Lam Dong

spots.name: Bahnar Orphanage
spots.desc: Visitors and donations welcome.

spots.name: Nghia
spots.desc: Solid vegetarian option with rice, pho, and bun dishes.

spots.name: Nhà hàng Nhật Bản Sakura Deli
spots.desc: Japanese restaurant of good quality.

spots.name: Hmong Sisters Bar
spots.desc: Has a pool table, darts and a computer with free Internet.

spots.name: Rockpile
spots.desc: A Marine outpost built on top of a huge outcropping. Though it's inaccessible, it's a prominent sight from the highway.

spots.name: Dak Rong Bridge
spots.desc: Midway along Hwy 9, and is the starting point of Hwy 15, one of the main branches of the Ho Chi Minh Trail, which leads south to the A Shau valley and the infamous "Hamburger Hill".
