Though not entirely legitimate, there is a monument commemorating it as a point on the Ho Chi Minh Trail, (called Đường Trường Sơn in Vietnamese).

spots.name: Mr Vinh
spots.desc: Mr Vinh, known to his American friends during the hostilities as "Davis", is an ex-ARVN military intelligence interpreter veteran from the war. He's old, speaks excellent English and is hospitable. At one stage, he interpreted for Colin Powell when he was a major general and General Westmoreland. He brings the sites of the DMZ alive. He is based in the Stop & Go Cafe in Hue but his cell number is…
spots.addr: Stop & Go Cafe - 03 Hung Vuong Hue City

spots.name: Son Ma Restaurant
spots.desc: This is the largest restaurant in Dak Nong province, with a capacity of up to 1000 people, relatively beautiful scenery.

spots.name: Mã Pí Lèng River Gorge
spots.desc: There are small tour boats here. The Mã Pí Lèng Pass above lies at an elevation of 1,500 meters.

spots.name: Hung Cuong Trading Company
spots.desc: Produces organic tea, certified according to USDA, EU, COR, IFOAM standards.

spots.name: Caves
spots.desc: There are a lot of caves around the island, though none of them are particularly impressive. Some cost money and may have optional guides. You can find them using the map or signs on the island.

spots.name: Ha Long Bay, Bai Tu Long Bay
spots.desc: Organised 2- or 3-day trips into Ha Long and Bai Tu Long Bay for kayaking, caving, swimming and diving. Book via the honest and fair Mr. Lu at the post office. Prices ~US$45 per person for 2-day, 1-night trip (assuming 4 people in group).

spots.name: Monkey Island
spots.desc: Several boats run day trips to nearby Monkey Island either in isolation or as part of a larger tour. The island apparently has monkeys, but only a few around the accommodation were in evidence. These animals are used to getting their food from either the guests or the bins, and therefore are not afraid of humans, so they might cause a problem. There is some accommodation on the island, which…

spots.name: Visiting Lan Ha Bay
spots.desc: Visit Lan Ha Bay with Serenity Premium Cruise are among few cruises designed in the neoclassical Indochine Style with a harmonious combination of Tradition and Modernity.
spots.addr: Lan Ha Bay, Cat Hai, Hai Phong

spots.name: Convenience store
spots.desc: Cheap convenience store. For example, Snickers costs 16,000 dong, unlike shops on the front that charge 25,000 dong.

spots.name: Mr. Zoom Hotel and Restaurant
spots.desc: Mostly good meals, but if he offers you an enormous (2 kg) round-looking crab creature thing, save your US$35.

spots.name: Phuong Phuong Restaurant
spots.desc: The restaurant has views of the sea, serves Vietnamese food and European food. Airy space, at an affordable price. Be wary of very long wait.

spots.name: Flightless Bird Bar
spots.desc: The original bar on the island, run by a New Zealander and going strong for 15 years. The drinks menu includes reasonably priced imported bottles of wine from various parts of the world as well as a straight to the point cheap drinks section. Darts upstairs.

spots.name: Rose Bar
spots.desc: Awesome drink menu, most cocktails 40,000. Brand new with nice atmosphere, and a really helpful, friendly young owner. Best cocktail prices in town, if you're sick of drinking beer all the time. Open late, rare in Cat Ba.

spots.name: Endangered Primate Rescue Centre
spots.desc: An important rehabilitation centre for Vietnam's critically endangered and majestic primates. Langurs, loris, and gibbon species are housed at the centre and include the critically endangered Delacour's Langur, golden-headed langur, Tonkin snub-nosed monkey and black crested gibbon.The centre was established in 1993 with the help of the Frankfurt Zoological Society and has grown to 100 animals in…
spots.price: 60,000VND Includes guide, Turtle Conservation, Museum, and Bird & Ungulates

spots.name: The Cuc Phuong Turtle Conservation Centre
spots.desc: It was established in 1998 and is home to some of the most endangered turtles in Vietnam. Six hundred turtles representing 15 of Vietnam’s 23 native species are bred at the centre and released back into the wild. At the centre it is possible to see hatchlings and adult turtles. The turtles at the centre are mostly specimens rescued from smugglers who supply the illegal trade in Vietnamese turtles…

spots.name: Carnivore and Pangolin Conservation Centre
spots.desc: Houses civets, including the rare Owston’s civet, and other small carnivores (including weasels, otters, and wild cats) and pangolins rescued from the wildlife trade. Renovated in early 2016, it's now open and welcomes its first visitors. Requires a guide.

spots.name: Botanical Garden
spots.desc: It's a good place to take a stroll and get an introduction to the region’s flora. Early in the morning you will hear birds singing, accompanied by perhaps a gibbon or two.
spots.price: Admission free. To open the garden's gate one needs to take keys at the information center

spots.name: Observation Lookout
spots.desc: Steep steps leading to 300 m height hill offering perfect views over the valley.

spots.name: Cave of Prehistoric Man
spots.desc: It is the site of one of the earliest discoveries of human habitation in Vietnam. Excavated in 1966, the cave revealed human graves, stone axes, pointed bone spears, oyster shell knives, and tools for grinding dating back 7,500 years. These artifacts have long been removed and the cave is open to tourists. The entrance to the cave is littered with picnic refuse and spent incense sticks, but if…

spots.name: Van Long Preserve
spots.desc: Near Cuc Phuong National Park is a preserve at Van Long where you can see Delacour’s langur in the wild. Cuc Phuong’s park headquarters can help arrange a trip to Van Long.

spots.name: Small local restaurant
spots.desc: Serves more or less the same food as restaurants inside the park.

spots.name: Old-growth trees
spots.desc: There are several impressively massive, hundreds-of-years-old trees, accessible on short walks down well-labelled side trails off of the main road, and one halfway along the longer Crocodile Lake trail. The tung tree on the Crocodile Lake trail is the most massive (if hiking solo at a non-busy time, you may regret not having anyone to take your picture with it), though the tung tree on the short…

spots.name: Heaven's Rapids
spots.desc: Perhaps the second-best scenic spot in the park, after Crocodile Lake. The river makes a horseshoe-bend here, with stereotypical jungle trees hanging over both banks, and the water rushing fast away from you on the downstream side.

spots.name: Crocodile Lake
spots.desc: At the end of the park's main popular longer-distance hiking trail (5- to 6-km walk, trailhead 9km from park headquarters), this is a large natural lagoon surrounded by green meadows at low-water times, and forest further back. You get a good, modestly-elevated view from the lodge and surrounding boardwalks, which are on tall stilts. Good for observing water birds and the namesake Siamese…

spots.name: Lower (Bến Cự) Rapids
spots.desc: A nice place to get a view of the river, at spot where it's relatively shallow, with a pretty landscape of rocks and water plants, at least during dry season when the water isn't too high. Accessible by a very short trail from the road's most prominent snack stand, not too far from park headquarters.

spots.name: "Botanical Garden"
spots.desc: Not so much a garden as a large section of native forest with trees and vines extensively labeled by species and family (Latin and Vietnamese names), with a network of short access trails for visitors wanting to get up close and personal with the jungle. The area extends roughly between the Lower Rapids and the Heaven's Rapids, on both sides of the road, though many trees beyond that area are…

spots.name: Nature Museum and Animal Rescue Center
spots.desc: A natural history museum very close to the park headquarters, which includes a park-run outdoor wildlife rehabilitation center for bears, gibbons, deer, and possibly other animals. Don't get your hopes up too much - previous visitors have reported that it was overcrowded because of limited funds (and lots of rescued bears), while at a recent glance in the gates it wasn't clear if there were many…

spots.name: Sam Mountain
spots.desc: Bike to Sam Mountain: rent a bike from your hotel (USD1-2) and ride 6 m to the base of Sam Mountain. It's an easy ride over flat paved and gravel road, just watch out for traffic. Walk on food from the base of the mountain, up the stairs to the top. Many viewpoints and cafe's with hammocks along the way to stop for a drink and a rest. Alternatively you can take a moto straight to the top of Sam…

spots.name: Tra Su Bird Sanctuary
spots.desc: As of January 2015 most hotels and travel agents are charging around USD34 for a two person trip to Tra Su (Includes moto drivers and boat fees). If you speak to any of the moto drivers around the covered market you should be able to hire one for around 150,000 - 200,000 dong per moto and can visit Sam Mountain or the Pagoda on the way back. Some of the drivers speak good English. Hiring a driver…
spots.price: 75,000 dong per person for 1½ hour visit (includes both speed and row boat ride)

spots.name: Thanh Tinh
spots.desc: A nice and clean local restaurant that serves vegan food. Friendly and English-speaking staff. They can also prepare take-away meals (handy for the journey on the slow boat to Cambodia). They charged 95,000 dong for a 'com phan', almost three times the usual price (March 2011).

spots.name: Bay Bong
spots.desc: Good food with a very long menu; locals and visitors eat here. The atmosphere isn't particularly romantic.

spots.name: Ha Tien Vegas
spots.desc: Hop over to the Cambodian side to visit, this casino/hotel. The entertainment resort has more than 100 slots, over 40 table games, Internet gaming and a Sports Book. For non-gamblers, Ha Tien Vegas Hotel provides a luxury hotel complemented by 24/7 room service, Chinese and international dining venues/cafes. Offers 24-hour shuttle service from the hotel and casino to downtown Hà Tiên.
spots.addr: Hà Tiên, Vietnam International Border Prek Chak

spots.name: Kayak Rental
spots.desc: Off the 28 near the coast you can easily rent kayaks for 80,000 dong. It's the best way to gain access to breathtaking views of the area.

spots.name: Ha Tien Fresh Seafood
spots.desc: Right on the beach is a great local seafood restaurant with a very private upstairs area overlooking the coast.

spots.name: Oasis Bar
spots.desc: Expat running the bar serving cold beer in cold glasses for less than 20,000 dong each. Also the only place where you can get cocktails, spirits and gin & tonic. They also serve coffee.

spots.name: Fish Sauce Plants
spots.desc: Where the famous nuoc mam (fish sauce) is produced. Big jars harbor the concoction that, after months in the blazing sun, is sold all over Vietnam to add some spice to the food.

spots.name: Red Sand Dunes
spots.desc: The famous Red Sand Dunes on the main coastal road a short distance north of the fishing town at the north end of Mui Ne Bay, about 10 km from the main resort strip. The whole region is fairly sandy, with orange sand threatening to blow onto the coastal road in some spots. The dunes that visitors visit are about 50 ha (1/2 km²) of open sand on a hillside with ten-meter undulations, staffed by…

spots.name: Fishing harbor
spots.desc: If you are staying on the resort strip in Ham Tien or Phu Hai wards, don't miss out to visit this once quiet "fishing village" but nowadays bustling town, at the northeast end of Mui Ne Bay. The coastal road leads straight into the town (with a left turn required at the first red light to continue up the coast). If you arrive during the dry "winter" season, don't miss the harbor overlook at the…

spots.name: Mui Ne Market
spots.desc: Further along into town, just off the main road, there is a colorful local market.

spots.name: Fairy Stream
spots.desc: The Fairy Stream is a little creek that winds its way through bamboo forests, boulders and the dunes behind the village, in parts resembling a miniature version of the Grand Canyon. Local children will want to accompany you to show you the way (and of course earn a dollar or so), but since you're just following the stream, there's little need. For the most part, the stream is about ankle-deep and…
spots.price: 10,000 dong (although entrance is officially free) and 5,000 dong for motorbike parking. Free from the north

spots.name: White Sand Dunes
spots.desc: The White Sand Dunes are approximately 45 km away from the Ham Tien tourist strip to the northeast, and some 24 km from the Red Sand Dunes and nearby resorts on the east side of the Mui Ne peninsula. Trips are offered by any tourist agency along the resort stretch for 4WD or quad drives, as well as by some resorts with their own vehicles. While too far away for a bicycle trip especially in…

spots.name: Bo Ke Street
spots.desc: This is a street full of local cafes that serve BBQ seafood. Prices are very cheap and choice is wide. Scallops with onion and garlic sauce are must-to-have here. If you're a fussy about hygiene, don't bother coming here.
spots.addr: 122 Nguyễn Đình Chiểu, Phường Hàm Tiến, Thành phố Phan Thiết, Bình Thuận

spots.name: Joe's
spots.desc: Joe's is the only place open 24/7 in Mui Ne. It's a cosy old farmhouse cafe offering Western fare. A Canadian developed the menu, and the pancakes with maple syrup (50,000 dong including coffee) are great. The sandwiches with home cut fries and salad (60,000 dong) are also recommended. Two movies are shown each evening in the pillow-filled loft. Free Wi-fi, exhibits and live performances. A great…
spots.addr: 86 Nguyen Dinh Chieu St, Ham Tien

spots.name: Dragon Beach - Lounge Bar & Club
spots.desc: Mui Ne's biggest disco with two dance floors, a pool, circular bar and its own access to the sea.

spots.name: Nirvana Beach Club (Line Up Bar)
spots.desc: Bar and nightclub popular with independent travelers. It has a large dance floor, good sound system, good food and friendly staff. During happy hour from 18:00 to 21:00 some cocktails cost just 30,000 dong, and for all cocktails you buy you get a second for free.

spots.name: Bat Temple
spots.desc: The monastery, while pleasing on its own, the main draw here are the fruit bats that live in the trees behind the temple. The monks protect them from the farmers in the area who consider them both a pest and a delicacy. Arrive about 1/2 hour before sunset to see the show begin. Any xe om in town can bring you here. There is also a Buddhist crematorium across the road from the temple.

spots.name: Clay Pagoda
spots.desc: This monastery was decorated by a monk sculptor who spent 60 years designing and installing thousands of statues into a colorful cacophony of Buddhist kitch. Notable features are: pillars with dragons on them, a baby white elephant, a white tiger, and golden turtles in the pond out back.

spots.name: Ngã Năm (5 fork intersection) Floating Market
spots.desc: Busiest at 05:00-06:00, but the market is held all day and all night on one fork of the river. You can rent a boat to go around for as little as USD2-3.

spots.name: Hung
spots.desc: This place has an extensive menu in Vietnamese. Drawing pictures sometimes helps, or bring a phrasebook along. The food is wonderful, and the open-air pavilion has a nice atmosphere. The staff is very helpful.

spots.name: Khánh Vi
spots.desc: Spacious restaurant, extensive menu, individual dishes from 65,000-150,000 dong. Attentive service.

spots.name: Truong Son National Cemetery
spots.desc: Vietnam's national war cemetery.

spots.name: Sunrise Cafe
spots.desc: Serving coffee, other drinks and breakfast.

spots.name: Duc Phuc 2 Restaurant
spots.desc: Vietnamese seafood restaurant.

spots.name: Beaches
spots.desc: Don't expect surfable waves, though!

spots.name: Noble House
spots.desc: Offers 2 for 1 cocktails and free pool.

spots.name: Metro 88
spots.desc: Poolside entertainment.

spots.name: Cham Island Tour
spots.desc: Pick up at hotel at 07:00, transfer to Cua Dai beach harbour by an air-con bus. Cruises to the Cham Islands board at 08:00, travelling by wooden boat for 1¼ hours or by speed boat for 30 minutes. On arrival, there are visits to Hai Tang Pagoda, the boat shelter, a local market at Bai Lang, then cruise to Bai Chong for swimming and snorkelling to see the coral reef before having lunch at a local…

spots.name: Cham Island Diving
spots.desc: PADI dive centre offering full range of services on the island from Hoi An: PADI courses, scuba diving and snorkelling, simple excursions and private cruise by wooden boat and speedboat, camping under the stars and home stay in authentic fisher village.
spots.addr: 88 Nguyen Thai Hoc str, Hoi An

spots.name: Karma Waters
spots.desc: Home stays inside private village homes at Bai Huong village. Daily rates USD120/person. All vegetarian meals included and return boat. Cham Island Day tour USD90. 08:00 departure. Snorkelling, swimming, vegetarian lunch. Also traditional Vietnamese sailing vessel, 10.5-m Ghe Nang, for cruises and sail training all year around the Cham Islands.

spots.name: Khe Sanh Battlefield Victory Museum
spots.desc: In the best preserved of the DMZ bases there is a museum featuring many photos from the war with a clear air of propaganda. The old airstrip remains, as do several American helicopters, a C130 transport and some North Vietnamese tanks.

spots.name: Khe Sanh Market
spots.desc: The market is far bigger than it would be otherwise for a town of its size, and with few tourists prices are cheap.

spots.name: Bắc Hà Sunday market
spots.desc: The Sunday market (which is much larger than the Sa Pa market) is a big, colorful bazaar overflowing with everything under the sun. Most visitors will probably be interested in the embroidered fabric handicrafts such as cellphone pouches, clothes, handbags, purses, and cushion covers, tablecloths and table runners sold by minority hill tribes. Also available are scarves; T-shirts; metal jewellery…

spots.name: Hoang Yen Restaurant
spots.desc: The food is average but it has a lively atmosphere as Sapa Green Tours arranges for its customers to dine there.

spots.name: Papa Russe
spots.desc: A friendly host, originally from Ukraine, offering pho (Vietnamese rice noodle soup) and fried rice dishes with meat, tofu, bamboo shoots and other vegetables, and so on, at socialist prices – 20,000 dong for everything! Sure, you still pay more than the locals, but the place offers quite good value for money and a friendly atmosphere. Come late, say 19:30, to get the best of Papa's own dinner.

spots.name: Restaurant Sunday Boulevard
spots.desc: Located on a quiet lane away from the main street, the restaurant serves reasonably priced noodle and rice dishes, fresh and deep-fried spring rolls, and other Vietnamese staples. There are two pleasant outdoor tables beside the street.

spots.name: Spring Fair Restaurant
spots.desc: Best spring rolls in town, and other freshly made local dishes at reasonable prices.

spots.name: Cong To Vo
spots.desc: An archway on the beach. Good place to see sunset.

spots.name: Hồ Thới Lới
spots.desc: A freshwater lake on top of the extinct volcano.

spots.name: Đỉnh Thới Lới
spots.desc: An extinct volcano with great view of the whole island.

spots.name: Thanh Son Restaurant
spots.desc: A reasonably priced restaurant catering mainly to tourists.

spots.name: Ba Na Hills
spots.desc: The hills are in the Truong Son mountain range about 25 km SW of Da Nang, at an elevation of 1,487 m. A 7-seater car with driver can be arranged easily in Lăng Cô and will take just over 1 hour each way at a cost of 600,000 dong. The hills have modern cable cars which give great views of Hai Van Pass to the left, Da Nang straight ahead, with China beach in the distance.
spots.addr: An Sơn Hamlet, Hoà Ninh Ward, Hoà Vang District

spots.name: Bach Ma National Park
spots.desc: Bach Ma is at an elevation of 1,450 m. The cooler temperature at the summit is very comfortable (about 7 C, cooler than low lying areas).

spots.name: Elephant Springs
spots.desc: A nice drive from Hwy 1 west approximately 5 km to the ticket booth. Here you pay to get in, then you drive a further 2 km to the parking lot. The springs are lined with little bamboo coverings along each side which cost about 20,000 dong for an area, unless you also purchase food from the person which they will generally waive the fee. You can purchase Hue beer for 10,000 dong as well as other…

spots.name: Hai Van Pass
spots.desc: This is the old highway prior to the construction of the 6.2-km tunnel. This road meanders over the mountain top between Da Nang and Lăng Cô. On the top are some breath taking views and some US outpost ruins from the war.

spots.name: Lang Co Springs
spots.desc: Lang Co Springs was just used by locals as access was limited before the new road was constructed around the lagoon. As of mid-2011, locals have started building bamboo shelters and selling food and drinks. A road and a parking area are under construction. A motorbike or bicycle can be taken from Lăng Cô up to the current parking area (at a local's house) and pay 5,000 dong. Then a 15 minute walk…

spots.name: Fishing Village
spots.desc: For the more adventurous are these ramshackle restaurants. During the summer months (Mar-Sep), this beach will have about 30 makeshift tents of bamboo, tarps, and lighting. Each place cooks and sells fresh seafood that is generally caught that day. It is an excellent experience. The cheapest and best seafood in the area.

spots.name: Sao Bien Restaurant
spots.desc: This restaurant has excellent seafood. Prices are reasonable. This restaurant is very popular and will always have buses parked outside with people from early morning through to late evening. Not to worry, there is plenty of seating either inside or outside overlooking the lagoon in the back.

spots.name: Lăng Cô Beach Resort
spots.desc: The Green Bar: 100 seats, on the beach. It is in an elevated position overlooking the beach and great place to have a few drinks and food. The Night Bar: 50 seats, rattan chairs and Vietnamese carved furniture. A pool table and dart board are inside. The resort has 84 guest rooms, 57 deluxe villas, suites and 27 budget rooms.

spots.name: Fairy Bosom
spots.desc: Two even hills lying side by side, with a bra made of trees.

spots.name: Khau Làn waterfall
spots.desc: A short and steep trail leads to a secluded 20 m waterfall and swimming hole.

spots.name: Quản Bạ Pass
spots.desc: The road to Quan Ba Heaven gate is winding, twisty crossing limestone mountains. At 1945 m, the viewpoints on both sides of the pass is one of the highlights of the park. From the top of the Heaven Gate, you can look down across a large valley of unending terraced fields, displaying a charming beauty like a paradise dimly visible through the clouds.

spots.name: Thâm Luông Waterfall
spots.local: Du Già Waterfall, Thác Du Già
spots.desc: Two large and several smaller cascades, one with a pond for swimming. Somewhat remote, the gravel path can be difficult to find.

spots.name: Dong Van Fort
spots.desc: Above Dong Van, the French built a fort in 1925. The remains, partially restored in 2013, overlook the entire town.

spots.name: Làng Văn Tourist Village
spots.desc: This village showcases minority culture. The turnoff to the right is clearly marked by a labeled gate.

spots.name: Tràng Hương
spots.desc: Village in the Nho Que valley. There are tour boats in the narrow river with turquoise water (round trip 1 hour) as well as kayak rentals.

spots.name: Dong Van market
spots.desc: On sale are local products made by Hmong, Han, Dao, Giay and Tay ethnic people. To reach the market on time they have to leave their homes very early in the morning or even one day earlier. At the market, people in different ethnic groups mingle with people from outside their small village to find their life-partners.
spots.addr: in the centre of Dong Van Old Quarter

spots.name: Ha Giang Sky Path
spots.desc: A 7-km hiking trail, high above the highway, near Ma Pi Leng Pass. It is accessible by stopping at the side of the road, and looks rather like a sidewalk going up the mountainside. Motorbikes are allowed for most of the road, and locals will ride past you if you are hiking. The end of the Sky Path is a gorgeous ~2km hike along a narrow trail cut into the karst cliff walls with stunning views of…

spots.name: Lung Tam Linen weaving products
spots.desc: Unique linen clothes, bags, handbags, scarfs, pillows, blankets, and purses. Every linen cloth weaving have traditional patterns, with the images bring the culture and color of the Hmong ethnic people by complicated indigo dyeing and beewax batik drawing process. Mrs Mai is the leader of Lung Tam linen weaving cooperative.
spots.addr: Lung Tam village, Quan Ba district

spots.name: Temples
spots.desc: There are two Buddhist temples in the town, virtually opposite one another though one sits atop a hill and the other near its base.

spots.name: Hieu Waterfall
spots.desc: The waterfall is known for its natural pools featuring multiple cascading levels and natural swimming spots, jungle scenery, and peaceful atmosphere. It is one of the best-known natural attractions in Pu Luong Nature Reserve, with water flowing through several levels of limestone rocks surrounded by forest and traditional stilt houses.

spots.name: Kho Muong village
spots.desc: A remote valley village surrounded by limestone mountains, home to Bat Cave, a limestone cave near the village. The village is surrounded by limestone mountains and rice terraces, and is known for its peaceful atmosphere and traditional Thai ethnic culture.

spots.name: Cai Be Floating Market
spots.desc: is a small and little visited floating market in Mekong Delta. It is held along the Tan Phong Island at the junction of Tien River in territory of three provinces Tien Giang, Vinh Long and Ben Tre. Every morning, hundreds of boats gather here to trade their local products, mainly fruit, creating a bustling fair. Different from other big floating market in the region, Cai Be is a retail market and…

spots.name: Dong Hoa Hiep Old House
spots.desc: There are quite some old houses in Dong Hoa Hiep Commune, Cai Be. Best preserved ones include Ba Duc Old House, Cai Huy Old House and Anh Kiet Old House. They were built in an old architecture typical in the region. Some were restored under a programme of Vietnamese government together with a Japanese organization, JICA.

spots.name: Mekong Lodge Riverside Restaurant
spots.desc: A semi-open air restaurant with nice settings and great view of Tien River, especially at sunset. Excellent food.

spots.name: The Cottage Hồ Tràm Hills
spots.desc: A private villa estate, 5 minutes from the beach and 10 minutes from Hamptons Pier. This 6-bedroom villa accommodates 12–16 guests and features: two outdoor Jacuzzi tubs, an outdoor BBQ area, a fully equipped kitchen, open-concept living/dining area with hill views, hammock garden & outdoor lounge zones.

spots.name: Lung Ho Fort
spots.desc: Ruins of a French military post constructed in 1935.

spots.name: Nhà Há Súng
spots.desc: A traditional extended family house, open to visitors.
